Dream In the go-big-or-go-home collective consciousness of Texas, no
ambition is deemed too reckless, no daydream too wild. Save perhaps one.
It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that
the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32
years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the
race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen
by national Democrats as one of the breakout stars of this cycle, is ahead
of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the state’s scandal-plagued attorney
general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30.
A survey from mid-September, the ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll,
also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four
points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most
dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as
well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the
state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas
pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all
that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the
University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look
at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you
still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned
for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of
much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone
Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and
self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an
18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted
worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an
anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014.
Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of
defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to
Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations,
Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be
the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue
wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points
in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern
University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico
has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has
staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to
fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott,
meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been
unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated
Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to
Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for
dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such
optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where
idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there
is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has
built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level
Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the
Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have
written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for
more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule
in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W.
Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot
more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke
Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the
founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on
the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run
because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really
talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground
states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t
since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join
President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring
farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of
state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s
county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left
unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating
budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s
been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the
satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a
century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence
among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly
forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March,
with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican
four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr.
Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later
acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included
bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed
him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr.
Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans.
In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino
voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with
Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass,
and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans
who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of
Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness
of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog
party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across
20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi
of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the
Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande
Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a
place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine
Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by
the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at
the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many
markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms.
Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville.
“There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,”
she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s
campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr.
Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself
statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with
a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however,
Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an
effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that
quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later
renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six
biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr.
Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the
sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine
archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a
bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr.
Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the
riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which
Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a
century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and
Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other
American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created
instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic
concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business
executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in
an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating
with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,”
he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for
Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote
for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything
for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a
lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture
in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National
Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall
and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to
disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200
landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while
other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of
a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed
operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about
data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s
Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others
in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have
failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican
sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for
Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing
the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the
negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly
into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which
are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is
in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could
pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the
voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid
at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus
tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor
neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025
on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner
who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an
early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant
County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader,
Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican
Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex
school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a
State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in
2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated
riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the
2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that
saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for
midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A
few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020,
straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could
impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has
frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only
eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail
is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s
list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump
administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the
“suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent
shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its
Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for
Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is
because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the
margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get
it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t
win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful.
Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and
Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded
by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in
all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of
these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could
energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not
bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those
names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the
Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said.
Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic
enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also
doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive
for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you
get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a
winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a
“gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight,
but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,”
he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely
won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are
reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”'

Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the 2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020, straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the “suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful. Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said. Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a “gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight, but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,” he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”' You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

body:
I'm endorsing three more Democrats for Congress. Let's help them finish strong in the final seven days.
#
We've got just one week until Election Day, Peter, and I've got three more candidates I'd like you to meet.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261027-1.JXSOkA&amount=5&refcode=em20261027-1265&t=1&akid=1265%2E34582%2E4Cui5L)
Today, I'm proud to endorse three more Democrats running for Congress in critical races across the country: Bob Brooks in Pennsylvania, Denise Powell in Nebraska, and Mitch Berman in Wisconsin.
**[With just seven days until Election Day, these candidates need our help to finish strong. If you're ready to join me in supporting them, chip in $5 or whatever works for you to Small Town PAC today →](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261027-1.JXSOkA&amount=5&refcode=em20261027-1265&t=2&akid=1265%2E34582%2E4Cui5L)**
I launched Small Town PAC back in April to put power back in the hands of our neighbors and help Democrats compete in places too many people have written off.
That means supporting teachers, nurses, veterans, labor leaders, and other working people who understand their communities because they've spent their lives serving them.
And these three candidates are exactly the kind of people I had in mind:
**Bob Brooks (PA-07)** is a firefighter and union leader who spent more than 20 years serving his community in eastern Pennsylvania. Now, he's running to bring that same commitment to working people to Congress.
**Denise Powell (NE-02)** is a mom, small business owner, and community leader who's spent years fighting to protect public schools and helping more Nebraskans run for office.
**Mitch Berman (WI-01)** grew up in a working-class family in rural Wisconsin and became an emergency room nurse. He's spent more than a decade caring for veterans and their families, and now he's running to take that experience to Washington.
These are folks who know what working families are up against. They've spent their careers looking out for their neighbors, and they're ready to do the same in Congress.
_But here's the deal: Endorsements alone don't win elections._
Our candidates are up against Republican opponents and wealthy special interests who would love nothing more than to keep working people out of power. And with just one week left, they need every resource they can get to reach voters and finish strong.
**[Peter, will you chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help Small Town PAC support Bob, Denise, Mitch, and our entire slate of endorsed candidates in these final seven days?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261027-1.JXSOkA&amount=5&refcode=em20261027-1265&t=3&akid=1265%2E34582%2E4Cui5L)**

We've got good people running. Now let's help them get across the finish line.
With gratitude,
Tim

Mitch Berman (WI-01) grew up in a working-class family in rural Wisconsin and became an emergency room nurse. He's spent more than a decade caring for veterans and their families, and now he's running to take that experience to Washington. These are folks who know what working families are up against. They've spent their careers looking out for their neighbors, and they're ready to do the same in Congress. But here's the deal: Endorsements alone don't win elections. Our candidates are up against Republican opponents and wealthy special interests who would love nothing more than to keep working people out of power. And with just one week left, they need every resource they can get to reach voters and finish strong. We've got good people running. Now let's help them get across the finish line. With gratitude, Tim

With crisp air, colorful leaves, pumpkin spice favorites, and the excitement of a new season, there are countless ways to enjoy this special time of year together. From decorating your home with pumpkins and fall crafts to creating a family gratitude tree, visiting a pumpkin patch or corn maze, and whipping up delicious seasonal treats, you don't have to plan an elaborate outing to make the season memorable. Cozy movie nights, family getaways, campfires, and simple evenings spent laughing together can become some of your children's favorite memories. And don't forget one important fall tradition! A Marine. A grieving dad. A promise to keep.
Peter,

I want to tell you why I'm running, and I want to do it straight.

My son was a United States Marine. He followed me into the Corps, and he came home proud of his service. Then one night, in our own hometown, he was murdered. For a long time after that, nothing happened. No leads, no arrests, no answers — just a quiet phone and a family trying to put one foot in front of the other. I do not have the words for what that kind of waiting does to a father.

[](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=a6cc25b509674a8b8601697e397865df&_e=EkfbnuEXGfyuxu0WZBgz1lUoO77myvhkeyGRbKPe35ZWf8VAu23Eiq1hdI-0PTn7aFFxWjyPf65i_X7Ay2yPw20Pi4EU3rI6340_SEYd4lzfl-0tykLNei8uCl8qk7vy_hz4twls0reP5NHawusbY5E75pBKV32cJ6eP52TpyKxS3JoiJE7MkLeLif0xwCmymcZhwKNqVC0Xwir0cqpbLgLwBXdW6cXZw8VZ1Hm8S_yuidTaapnE3h8LI3QxugtnyR7yE4HndBKSS1ZCKLI0QGDwJ66_vb1EtS7rNRYsW9o0d_s7wP0g6sUj_c34YDX6FuOztCVC9TPFDlzSV1GgthzQwdlSxhoYcb_wnSwwKDBn0CEZ3ngwCgXLsdQaOv5LfFFGe6pavWBdzvrBBbh1ZQpP9iw7jR3VrLbrc-7CdgNLzkOut7xaihaCWHcwbUJ6OJVozriCBXlIgCaND6XXIF-uO35TPW-UN0xsStshMbLFv-oViUpn8FNy-pgw7giq7EqcSc7xA1MXIN5qxuGuFw%3D%3D)
But I learned one thing in those years. Sitting still was not going to bring my son back, and it was not going to keep another family from getting the knock on the door that I got. So I made him a promise. No other dad would bury his child the way I buried mine. Not if I could help it.

I ran for Hemet City Council on that promise, and I won. Every day since, I have gone to work on public safety — better policing, cleaner streets, real consequences for the people who hurt our families. We have made real progress. But the truth is, a city can only do so much when Washington is asleep at the wheel.

**That is why I'm running for Congress.**

[ **STAND WITH JOE TODAY** ](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=a6cc25b509674a8b8601697e397865df&_e=EkfbnuEXGfyuxu0WZBgz1lUoO77myvhkeyGRbKPe35ZWf8VAu23Eiq1hdI-0PTn7aFFxWjyPf65i_X7Ay2yPw20Pi4EU3rI6340_SEYd4lzfl-0tykLNei8uCl8qk7vy5TLwQibzz0h8IfRHswns9gdr5jzc6iVKr8o8HKTCvZKhNR0iIAozokg-OUmLMVA1IcOwaCUm0D2i2OPxsCqFwEDEMS8I7n7Pq3JXuQlSIqJTPELqlcqLTNiqu5xCFxmAY-G9EjSAg5xWjtAJpfA919KEnBDEr0FkILmaDnoYjBUuSR9SeGYFpTZyj9QZ3dOZMfuo5-jbuqL24tEV6HDRF0kHpTAL2YRsd440p_uIdIgmLKMvEXGutWec6ve6GbyUUlP8XxOMpVgrOMCYQZcRXVp65exmupO30qNqeohy63wu_PQwxtyUbQE9DvhmJie5pXsfE1Mlr9b3L-157JzBnQYUp28NW6l4vvTHg0j5B36zK5xA5nuVITS4rrVtAFX6yzU3mhoEVDByxB4_W5HrGHjRCMQABbZzXALi7ahYBzY%3D)
---

Crime is up. Our borders are open. Career politicians in D.C. cash their checks and look the other way. They don't see what we see. They don't lose what families like mine have lost. I do, and I am not going to stop fighting until that changes.

I'm a Marine. I'm a father. I'm a small business owner who knows what it takes to make a payroll for 22 years. I'm not slick, I'm not polished, and I’m not for sale. I am one man who made a promise to his son, and I am keeping it the only way I know how.

**But I cannot get to Washington on my own, Peter.** **[A gift of $10 helps me knock on another door. A gift of $25 helps me put another ad on the air. Whatever you can spare brings us one step closer to a country where no parent ever gets the call I got.](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=a6cc25b509674a8b8601697e397865df&_e=EkfbnuEXGfyuxu0WZBgz1lUoO77myvhkeyGRbKPe35ZWf8VAu23Eiq1hdI-0PTn7aFFxWjyPf65i_X7Ay2yPw20Pi4EU3rI6340_SEYd4lzfl-0tykLNei8uCl8qk7vy5TLwQibzz0h8IfRHswns9gdr5jzc6iVKr8o8HKTCvZKhNR0iIAozokg-OUmLMVA15SnJPrUjmSZcHPYKMjXWz8MImRmR1lrWNXJPGRR7n-36mUfJpAbzV7pK-nIRIpefIk593FDCEf0YXc_0amaziBC0ac2Ly9Wjwg-szDDF00lY44jFG8MITy0apPITUyVkwdhzYk21RyboG27QIAFZfgNhm0nNqQklIOYmJCnnaZyhRBzzky6lGlAAq5UGvUXBAWJTAd1IvHPJAUe6VBfWySm2h0EJGKDkjGOfAzb-VUd0IUV2Zc7E-soHnumKnEWRjGJF77tq4ARtnsI1ad6u-uyMoX6hMAB5SzdWgG6QkvLIzKrCnZvhjlfUmQkVjb2WSz2E0V9kxL0V3seGCS8gUIeVvtSnp_aPo8xPdPrFC3w%3D)**

[ **CHIP IN $25 TO HELP JOE WIN** ](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=a6cc25b509674a8b8601697e397865df&_e=EkfbnuEXGfyuxu0WZBgz1lUoO77myvhkeyGRbKPe35ZWf8VAu23Eiq1hdI-0PTn7aFFxWjyPf65i_X7Ay2yPw20Pi4EU3rI6340_SEYd4lzfl-0tykLNei8uCl8qk7vy5TLwQibzz0h8IfRHswns9gdr5jzc6iVKr8o8HKTCvZKhNR0iIAozokg-OUmLMVA1iwQrjrHLYXRa2uuouu_EIOKAsAHRE9ghaoxyMmeZWdkBbd7PGYrLrZrz3yydGP2GAVcMGj5UDJBLQp6G566oTRid4gXqJ5oEhOBN8DQ3dRtNDImk-6TKyuY187bre6KLQ4YGUAkL5C2vAI8xNBhCz6i8CT294yux3d1nrxWWHD1s6D5JskWloCHwlS2gCAuHkNWlXsAITJkpobgehG8a5jstXRGMkZqS0Ihd4VEMRF4CHuS5KXDOBsXeF4VmqylZ13ql8IHEnSKVZF2qCg1LxlI2z64INcd13mhDpA4WsHfwOvMyc8BKzAVenwPyWbBpRlpel700nqHVoaW4yrpnPZJ70kyZLA7ZWird7x3Ux_c%3D)

I will never get my son back. I have made my peace with that. But I can spend the rest of my life making sure another family does not live my nightmare — and with your help, I will.

**[Thank you for reading this, and thank you for standing with me.](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=a6cc25b509674a8b8601697e397865df&_e=EkfbnuEXGfyuxu0WZBgz1lUoO77myvhkeyGRbKPe35ZWf8VAu23Eiq1hdI-0PTn7aFFxWjyPf65i_X7Ay2yPw20Pi4EU3rI6340_SEYd4lzfl-0tykLNei8uCl8qk7vy5TLwQibzz0h8IfRHswns9gdr5jzc6iVKr8o8HKTCvZKhNR0iIAozokg-OUmLMVA1C8_L22pvZd3llFwZFMdv5I0FLaEE1gPPuQJ51S8A8_SlBvjx0G7dbPlBThHN8VVmkVIlh4oMLjWVnK04wFgevfHP7g94O7MOTNKCKFgi-7TKItuHgkrQ7sKKKmHqWtSfvzZc8vYkizllowZAL_jMDtSFghQuM4ab34_a8FcvoLrLbfDj3bHbDlwdYV-qeSKrxCo55j-IF2pFtAtRK5ZmLsLWSZdRuLG63iWuFbv6N1vW3PVQ9Q4FLk_4dCxCqoSsXSlqbMFg-J-c2vGhlxLfwvGYML6ayRXfZ6xdMGDklOcR6mVqHSG6KvP-AwOf3wfO0DOugci4EacyuTsBmxxI0g6IHmMFF26Ao77TN4HjY4A%3D)**

I'm not slick, I'm not polished, and I’m not for sale. I am one man who made a promise to his son, and I am keeping it the only way I know how. But I cannot get to Washington on my own, Peter. I will never get my son back. I have made my peace with that. But I can spend the rest of my life making sure another family does not live my nightmare — and with your help, I will. Semper Fi, Joe Males Sergeant, USMC Veteran Candidate for Congress, CA-25 P.S. I made a promise to my son. Help me keep it. Help Flip California’s 25th Joe Males is a Marine, a father, and a fighter. Help him take the fight to Washington. PAID FOR BY MALES FOR CONGRESS (C) 2026 Males for Congress, All rights reserved.

**Janoo’s Solution for Housing is to “Limit Residents and Businesses”**
A recent WPTZ report summarized Janoo’s “post-growth” plan to address housing costs in Vermont the following way:
**“To address Vermont’s housing crisis,_Janoo says she wants to limit the number _****_of residents and businesses moving to the state._****”**
* Source: NBC5, WPTZ, _Who is Amanda Janoo, the Democratic Candidate for Vermont governor_ , Cusanelli and Maloney, Monday, October 26, 2026

**Now, compare Janoo’s position to Governor Phil Scott’s** : “As I say all the time, **we need more taxpayers, not more taxes** ...we know mortgages and rents are unaffordable for many. Housing costs drive people out of Vermont and prevent families, workers, and good jobs from moving here. **To me, the issue is obvious.** ”
\-- Governor Phil Scott To paraphrase Forest Gump ... that’s all we have to say about that.

body:
But honestly, I need all the help I can get this year.

| I don’t often write personal messages like this, and I hate to add another message to your inbox, but honestly, I need all the help I can get this year.
I bet you get dozens of texts and emails a day questioning your GOP loyalty, threatening you, or even making you pay to take a poll on voter ID. I promise to never do that to you.
I’m taking the time to write this because I want to be perfectly honest about what's at stake this year.
So here it is, no flashy colors, donation buttons, or fake matches.
I hope you’ll read this entire message.
---
From: Congressman Gabe Evans
First and foremost, thank you.
I've been a lot of things in life: an Army Black Hawk helicopter pilot, a rancher, and a cop.
But never in a million years did I think I'd have the honor of fighting for our Conservative movement in Congress.
Your support has gotten me where I am today, and I never take that for granted.
But it wasn't some cakewalk.
I ran for Congress in deep-blue Colorado, where Republicans hadn't flipped a Democrat-held seat in over a decade.
Against all odds, I won and became the voice for thousands of Conservatives stuck under the thumb of Radical Democrat rule.
It's not a responsibility I take lightly.
My race was decided by just 2,500 votes and was one of the most expensive House races in the country in 2024.
Now, just two years later, Democrats are looking for their revenge.
[](https://trk.emails.evansforcolorado._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMjdfWFEtMUIuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDcyOTYzLTkyMDImdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDI3X1hRLTFCLjExMDExN190MjA3Mjk2My05MjAyIn0/9nokeIOvnnn_oKz5Yl2bmw)They've already poured millions into this race and are planning an ad blitz to bury my campaign and drown out my message with lies and smears.
They want people to forget what happened when they were in charge.
Under the control of Radical Democrats, we saw illegal immigrants pouring in by the tens of thousands, crime spiraling out of control, and even armed Venezuelan gang members taking over apartment complexes at gunpoint.
As a former cop, watching that happen in my community broke me.
I know how Democrats run things, and I know we can never go back.
Unfortunately, my seat is one of the Democrats' TOP TARGETS, and polling shows this race is a true toss-up that could be decided by even fewer votes than last time.
That's why I'm writing to you today.
Because you're all I've got to help fend off the Democrats' money machine.
The only way I can keep this seat red is with the support of Patriots like you.
[Could you help me keep this seat red by pitching in anything you can today?](https://trk.emails.evansforcolorado._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249My8_YW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMjdfWFEtMUIuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDcyOTYzLTkyMDImdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDI3X1hRLTFCLjExMDExN190MjA3Mjk2My05MjAyIn0/b-uR3XBvOCd5eDWVDPQ4BQ)
Remember, this seat was decided by just 2,500 votes. That's about 1%.
Democrats know the key to taking back the House Majority runs through seats like mine, and they're prepared to spend whatever it takes to flip them.
I can't match their millions on my own.
But with enough Patriots standing together, we can beat them again.
So if you're able to give today, I would be incredibly grateful.
[You can use this secure link to pitch in and help this retired Army vet stay in Congress.](https://trk.emails.evansforcolorado._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMjdfWFEtMUIuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDcyOTYzLTkyMDImdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDI3X1hRLTFCLjExMDExN190MjA3Mjk2My05MjAyIn0/R14B14zuh9U6M2tQ33sMTA)
Thank you for standing with me.
Congressman Gabe Evans (CO-08)

**In just the first two weeks of October, this campaign raised $99,847 from more than 200 individual donors. Almost all of them live right here in Wisconsin.**

Last Thursday night, around 8:00 p.m., Gina, our campaign manager, filed our latest FEC report. She filed it from a bar in Wausau, laptop open, with a big smile on her face (you can see the photo below).

Hi everyone. This is Kelly Morrison. We’re one week out from Election Day, and our voter turnout push is in full swing. But even though it’s firing on all cylinders, it’s not fully funded – **there’s more we can do**. I know this team always steps up when it matters most, so I sat down to write this email asking for your support. But then my husband John jumped in and informed me that he is a very effective fundraiser for my campaign. In fact, he suggested that if _he_ asked you, we might even raise more. I clearly can’t just take his word for it, so we decided to put it to the test. We’re both sharing messages with you in this email, and we’ll each ask you to donate – whoever raises more will have bragging rights for all time, and of course, every penny will go directly toward the critical work left to win the midterms.I get to go first and I’ve already taken up some of your time, so I’m making my ask very short and to the point: This midterm election is one of the most consequential of our lifetime. What happens one week from today will determine the damage Trump can do over the next two years – and with the possibility of a Supreme Court vacancy, it will also determine the damage his legacy can do over the next several decades or even generations. I’ve been lucky to get a front-row seat to her incredible work in the state legislature and in Congress. But I’m certainly not the only one who knows all that – everyone who has ever met or talked with Kelly could say the exact same thing. _Because the truth is, Kelly treats every constituent like a member of her own family. _ **She fights just as hard for you as she would for herself, or for our kids, or for me – because that’s just who she is.** I’m willing to bet you agree that Congress is in _desperate_ need of that kind of compassionate, effective leader right now. Friend, Early on in the campaign, w _hen reporters finally caught up with Marsha Blackburn_ to ask her why she refusesd to step onto a debate stage or even answer unscripted questions from voters and journalists, her answer was _ **"I'm talking to Tennesseans every day."**_ _****_**_Really?_** Because it’s been nearly _**a decade since she held an open, public in-person town hall**_. Instead of answering to everyday Tennesseans, she hides behind invite-only corporate fundraisers, tightly scripted media appearances, and pre-screened phone calls where no one can challenge her record. When she says she’s talking to Tennesseans, she means high-dollar donors and political insiders. **Well, I actually talk to everyday Tennesseans every single day— _and here is what they are telling me:_**
* **They are suffocating under everyday costs.** They want real relief—like eliminating the state grocery tax, capping prescription drug costs, and lowering monthly energy bills—not more tax giveaways for out-of-state corporations.
* **They are furious about state politicians starving our public schools.** Parents and teachers across all 95 counties are tired of voucher schemes that strip millions out of neighborhood classrooms to subsidize private school tuition for wealthy families.
* **They want healthcare they can actually rely on. **They’re tired of local hospital closures and healthcare monopolies like Ballad Health driving up medical prices while cutting patient services. They want us to expand Medicaid and break up healthcare cartels.
* **They are sick of corruption, corporate graft, and backroom deals. **They want leaders who answer to working people—not out-of-state nuclear waste companies or pharmaceutical lobbies.

_**Marsha Blackburn can dodge debates, skip town halls, and ignore the public, but she cannot avoid the voters on Election Day.**_ Tennessee doesn’t need another career politician who treats voters like a photo op. We need a Governor who stands with working families, listens to local communities, and shows up to fight for them every single day. clean_body: | Friend, Early on in the campaign, w hen reporters finally caught up with Marsha Blackburn to ask her why she refusesd to step onto a debate stage or even answer unscripted questions from voters and journalists, her answer was "I'm talking to Tennesseans every day." **Really? Because it’s been nearly a decade since she held an open, public in-person town hall. Instead of answering to everyday Tennesseans, she hides behind invite-only corporate fundraisers, tightly scripted media appearances, and pre-screened phone calls where no one can challenge her record. When she says she’s talking to Tennesseans, she means high-dollar donors and political insiders. Well, I actually talk to everyday Tennesseans every single day— and here is what they are telling me: They are suffocating under everyday costs. They want real relief—like eliminating the state grocery tax, capping prescription drug costs, and lowering monthly energy bills—not more tax giveaways for out-of-state corporations. They are furious about state politicians starving our public schools. Parents and teachers across all 95 counties are tired of voucher schemes that strip millions out of neighborhood classrooms to subsidize private school tuition for wealthy families. They want healthcare they can actually rely on. They’re tired of local hospital closures and healthcare monopolies like Ballad Health driving up medical prices while cutting patient services. They want us to expand Medicaid and break up healthcare cartels. They are sick of corruption, corporate graft, and backroom deals. They want leaders who answer to working people—not out-of-state nuclear waste companies or pharmaceutical lobbies. Marsha Blackburn can dodge debates, skip town halls, and ignore the public, but she cannot avoid the voters on Election Day. Tennessee doesn’t need another career politician who treats voters like a photo op. We need a Governor who stands with working families, listens to local communities, and shows up to fight for them every single day. Can you believe it's election season again? Election Day is next Tuesday, November 3, and early voting is already underway in many states. With just one week to go, the political landscape looks very different from the one that brought Republicans back to power.
President Trump's approval rating has fallen to[ 33 percent](https://substack.com/redirect/22292f0a-3b9b-4119-9286-581b738b372b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as his war with Iran has grown[ increasingly unpopular](https://substack.com/redirect/8f4b5e92-4a98-48ec-8b3b-9508b548bc7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Meanwhile, rising gas prices and stubborn inflation are hitting American families and small businesses at home, and some of the voters who helped put Republicans in power are beginning to look for something different.
The parallels with the 2006 midterms are hard to miss. By the fall of that year, George W. Bush's approval rating had fallen to about[ 38 percent](https://substack.com/redirect/5039737c-4cb7-4539-ae9f-cffb38dd7b35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as an unpopular Iraq War and growing economic anxiety weighed on Republicans. Democrats went on to gain[ 31 House seats](https://substack.com/redirect/55e70a08-55b6-4bf5-a7e8-b5d0ce5100aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), winning control of the chamber for the[ first time in 12 years](https://substack.com/redirect/89241267-6544-4973-a2ef-7e231006895a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and breaking through in districts that had long seemed out of reach.
I was one of the unlikely candidates who helped make that happen. At 31, fresh from Iraq, I ran in a[ Republican-leaning](https://substack.com/redirect/957156d8-6512-43fb-a25a-942f86a3364b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Bucks County, Pa., district that Bush had carried two years earlier. Washington saw me as a long shot.
We proved them wrong.
We won by[ 1,521 votes](https://substack.com/redirect/6e8119a0-9dc7-4b23-ae6d-633914bdee80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- 50.3 percent to 49.7 percent -- becoming the first Iraq War veteran elected to Congress and flipping a Republican-held seat in one of the defining upset victories of that election. It was a historic win in a historic election, and it gave me a firsthand understanding of what happens when the political ground suddenly shifts beneath a party's feet. More importantly, it taught me a lesson Democrats should remember now: a favorable political climate can create an opening, but it cannot build a majority on its own. Winning still requires persuading voters who did not start out on the Democratic side and then leading them to a better America.
The shift is showing up on the map. The[ Cook Political Report](https://substack.com/redirect/89bad158-091f-4ced-b3e7-1dbcf0a97def?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recently moved Texas and Iowa from "Lean Republican" to "Toss Up," expanding the core Senate battlefield from four states to six. The Senate itself, once widely viewed as out of reach for Democrats, is now[ increasingly competitive](https://substack.com/redirect/bc3b2cd8-6a4f-4075-a6bf-8d2ca76e984f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But a favorable map is not a coalition. Democrats still have to persuade the voters who are making those races competitive.
The discontent extends beyond Democrats.[ Seventy-one percent](https://substack.com/redirect/22292f0a-3b9b-4119-9286-581b738b372b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Americans disapprove of President Trump's handling of the cost of living, including four in 10 Republicans. Among[ independents](https://substack.com/redirect/7429d069-8f41-4564-a85e-8e816811ba9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Democrats currently hold a significant nine point advantage on the congressional ballot. Those numbers should encourage Democrats. They should also be a warning.
A record 45 percent of Americans identified as independents in 2025, according to[ Gallup](https://substack.com/redirect/05af9112-0bc7-4874-9016-1ce9eb52330f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), while just 27 percent called themselves Democrats and the same share called themselves Republicans. Independents are the fastest growing political party in the country. These are also voters who move the needle:[ independents favored Joe Biden in 2020](https://substack.com/redirect/c2e1c38e-e5d1-486d-ac85-dafafba65cee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by 9 points but[ split evenly between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump](https://substack.com/redirect/901c9e79-c021-4517-929c-118656899e78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four years later. If American politicians want their votes, they have to earn them.
That was certainly true in Bucks County in 2006. More than 2,000 volunteers knocked on roughly 160,000 doors for our campaign. We competed in Republican communities because there was simply no other way to win. Many of the voters I needed had supported George W. Bush. Some had voted for him twice. In purple Bucks County,
My job was not to lecture those voters about why they had been wrong to support Bush. It was to understand why they had voted the way they did, tell them what I believed and give them a reason to make a different choice. Yes, I was making the case for why the incumbent should be fired. But I also had to make the case for why I should be hired. That sounds obvious, but increasingly, it is not. Much of modern politics, particularly online, is organized around affirmation rather than persuasion. Too often, it has become a form of political infotainment. Candidates are rewarded for proving that they understand the language, priorities and enemies of their own faction to gin up their base for donations and support. The electorate in a Democratic or Republican primary is not the electorate candidates will face in November. In districts like Bucks County, [independents are more than 18% of the electorate](https://substack.com/redirect/fc702fae-be01-4ed7-8420-3b9c462006c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with Democrats composing 40% and Republicans 42%, so the general election requires a much broader appeal, especially after Donald Trump edged out Joe Biden here two years ago.
This does not mean Democrats should become ideologically uniform or sprint toward the center on every issue once they win next Tuesday. This is especially true in purple counties and states like Pennsylvania -- we are one of only three states with US senators from different parties and a divided state government. Pluralism, even within one's own party, does not require everybody to believe the same thing. It requires something more basic: respect for people who disagree with you. Millions of Americans voted for Donald Trump because they believed he would improve their lives. Many are now disappointed. Democrats should simply ask whether the president they supported has delivered and explain what they would do differently. Those voters need somewhere else to go.
A voter should not have to apologize for his 2024 ballot before he is welcomed into a Democratic coalition in 2026. Give people a reason to change their minds without demanding that they first confess they were bad people for having held them. Respecting Republican voters is not the same as excusing Republican leaders, and Democrats should criticize the president forcefully where they believe he has failed.
That was one of the great lessons of 2006. The national environment opened the door for Democrats, but voters still had to walk through it. In purple Bucks County, enough Republicans and independents decided that they could disagree with me about some things and still trust me to represent them.
The political climate is once again moving in Democrats' direction. But politics can be fickle, and favorable conditions alone do not win elections. People do.
Some on the political right are discrediting polling even though the writing is on the wall as Congress has deferred to the executive branch, while many on the left don't accept the fact that while we're heading toward another change election, it's not necessarily because Americans want dramatic policy changes. The last six federal elections have all resulted in a change of party control in the House, Senate, or the White House, and next week - November 3rd -- will make it seven change elections in a row. And while most Americans want change, it better be the kind that responsibly ends the unnecessary war in Iran and makes the cost of living much more affordable, both at the pump and at home.

Whatever happens next Tuesday, let's hope we use this as an opportunity to remember God gave us each two ears, two eyes, but only one mouth for a reason - to harness the skill to truly listen and respect viewpoints that aren't necessarily our own.
The people whose minds differ from Democrats or Republicans are not their enemies. They are our fellow Americans. We should respect them enough to ask for their votes and to give them a reason to believe in political public service again.

Peter, this is not good:
News broke that a Trump-aligned super PAC is launching a NEW seven-figure attack ad buy against me – just after he was here in person for another MAGA rally with my opponent, Michael Whatley.
**If you care about flipping this seat and the Senate exactly one week from today, I urgently need your help to fight back against the new onslaught of dishonest attacks.[_Will you chip in $5 or any amount right away to help us reach our last end-of-month goal before Election Day?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1705&amount=5&t=8&akid=4989%2E124072%2ELFn4Sy)**

President Trump is going all in to defeat me, and there’s a simple reason why:
If we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will lose our chance at taking back the Senate for the people and putting a check on his abuses of executive power. If the GOP can just keep Senate control, he’ll get to carry out his cruel agenda unfettered in his final two years in office.
That’s why both he _and_ JD Vance came for two back-to-back rallies in NC – and now, their super PAC allies are spending millions in a last-ditch effort to buy Whatley’s way to the Senate.
With so much at stake, I need your help to prove that their desperate attempts to discredit me and our grassroots movement are too little, too late.
**If folks like you chip in now and help us have our biggest fundraising day of the month, we can turn things around. If not, we risk letting our slim lead slip away.**
[**_That’s why I’m personally asking, Peter: Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can today so we can reach our $5 million goal, respond to the renewed MAGA attacks, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate for the people?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1705&amount=5&t=13&akid=4989%2E124072%2ELFn4Sy)
Thank you so much. I’m grateful for whatever you’re able to contribute.
Roy Cooper

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

clean_body: Friend, My name is Emily, and I'm a ballot chaser for Turning Point PAC in Arizona. That means every day, I show up, knock on doors, have conversations with potential voters, and chase down ballots before Election Day. I need to tell you what I'm seeing out here, because I don't think most people understand how close this really is. Arizona is not lost.Not even close. But it is not safe either. A new poll just showed Katie Hobbs up by 4 points over Andy Biggs. Four points. That is the entire ballgame, sitting right there behind the doors I have not knocked on yet. Turning Point PAC is not like anything else in this space. They take decades of grassroots organizing and put real people, like me, into these communities well before Election Day. We build relationships. We knock on the same doors more than once. We chase every ballot, mail-in or in person, because every single one counts. This is the vision Charlie Kirk built. People on the ground, having real conversations, changing real minds. And it is working! But I cannot do this alone, and neither can the 700 of us out here across Arizona. I 'm seeing momentum on the ground, but we have so many more voters to cover. We can't do it without your continued support. Every $50 you give sponsors a ballot chaser like me for one full day. That's about 75 doors and 25 real conversations with voters who haven't made up their minds yet, and who deserve to hear from us before it's too late. **Tuesday, October 27, 2026 -**_****_
_**Iran:** Iran hails emerging regional order without foreign intervention after Tehran meeting. Oman says excluding Iran from Gulf security has been a fundamental mistake. Iran says oil tanker caught fire after striking naval mines east of Hormuz. UK charges two British men in Iran-linked investigation at U.S. bomber base._
_**Palestine:** Six-year-old girl dies of wounds from Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis. Israel bars delegates from Birzeit University conference as settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank. UN commission finds Israel continuing genocide in Gaza despite ceasefire, committing crimes against humanity in West Bank. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud prepares election fraud claims as paid teams monitor Palestinian voters._
_**Yemen:** Ansarallah says Egypt's pledge of military support for Saudi amounts to a "declaration of war." Ansarallah claims strike on Saudi oil refinery, military aircraft._
_**Lebanon:** Israel shells towns across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire._
_**U.S.:** FTC orders Anthropic executives to testify in consumer-harm probe. DOJ charges former FBI director James Comey with leaking information. Court rejects DOJ attempt to cast doubt on 20,000 California ballots. AP: ICE detained mentally ill man for almost a year despite records showing he was born in the U.S._
_**International:** Right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro effectively concedes defeat in Brazil, lacking U.S. intervention and fearing prosecution. Egyptian court orders closure of leading news outlet Mada Masr, detains editor. Drone strike in RSF-held territory kills at least 21, injures 40; western nations warn of famine. Congo exceeds 10,000 Ebola cases. 89,000+ people evacuated in eastern India ahead of Cyclone Arnab. Attacks in Ethiopia kill at least 60 Orthodox Christians. Jordan strikes Syria in response to Karak church attack, killing at least seven. Romania accuses Russia-backed actors of sabotaging weapons factory. Colombia to withdraw from Hague Group coalition over stance on Israel._
**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *
# Iran
* **Iran hails emerging regional order without foreign intervention after Tehran meeting:** Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey [met](https://substack.com/redirect/1b88b020-243e-4cce-8c77-6512a309d364?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iranian leaders in Tehran on Monday for talks on regional security and escalating tensions, with Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei declaring that "a new atmosphere is emerging in the region."
* Rezaei said the sides held "very good" talks and agreed that West Asia's security should be managed by regional states, without foreign intervention. The "results of the Iranian nation's resistance" are becoming more tangible "day by day," he said.
* The four countries said they would "continue the dialogue," and officials called it the first in an expected series of meetings, though no date has been set.
* **Oman says excluding Iran from Gulf security has been a fundamental mistake:** Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi [criticized](https://substack.com/redirect/218a7951-e60f-4911-8e53-c5d7d112985e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) decades of Gulf security arrangements built around excluding Iran and relying on foreign military powers, calling for a new regional security framework that includes Tehran. "Perhaps the most damaging of the priorities imposed on the region from the outside has been the requirement that Iran be excluded," he said during a lecture at Cambridge University.
* This, he said, created an unstable system based on the "entirely false perception" of fundamental antagonism between Iran and Arab Gulf states. "There is no such fundamental antagonism," he said, adding that any security architecture excluding Iran is "inherently unstable" and "structurally unsound."
* He also said that Oman and Iran had developed the outline of a temporary arrangement to restore navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, but said implementation would require compromises by both Tehran and Washington.
* He maintained that a U.S.-Iran nuclear agreement had been within reach before the U.S.-Israeli war began on February 28, an assessment Oman continues to stand by.
* **Iran says oil tanker caught fire after striking naval mines east of Hormuz:** An oil tanker caught fire after striking naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy said Tuesday. The vessel had entered a prohibited area with its tracking systems switched off, according to Iranian state media.
* Separately, Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority announced that all vessels belonging to South Korean shipping company Sinokor will face legal action beginning November 1, accusing the company of repeatedly violating passage regulations in the Strait.
* The authority, established by Tehran to manage vessel transit requests through the waterway, said Sinokor had recorded the highest number of crossing violations over the past three months and that "appropriate actions" had already been taken against at least seven of its vessels.
* **UK charges two British men in Iran-linked investigation at U.S. bomber base:** Two British nationals were [charged](https://substack.com/redirect/aa5c6e6f-c94f-4856-a57d-b17cdca7f1ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) under the UK's National Security Act following an investigation into a September security incident at RAF Fairford, a British airbase used by U.S. bombers. One man is charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, while another is charged with entering a prohibited site for a purpose prejudicial to the UK.
* RAF Fairford has been used by the U.S. to deploy bombers to the Middle East, including after Britain authorized its use for strikes against Iran. The U.S. withdrew its bombers following the incident.
* British counterterrorism police said they believe several recent incidents were directed by the Iranian state. Iran has denied involvement.

# Palestine
* **Six-year-old girl dies of wounds from Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis:** A six-year-old Palestinian girl [died](https://substack.com/redirect/a9f6ab9b-26e8-4afe-a214-eb7449e0b4c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday morning from wounds sustained after being shot by Israeli forces in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis, southern Gaza, WAFA reported.
* Over the past 24 hours, six Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks and 32 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, is now 74,561 killed, with 175,759 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,565 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,640, while 845 bodies have been recovered.
* **Israel bars delegates from Birzeit University conference as settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank:**
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [continued](https://substack.com/redirect/3a65e494-62d2-403c-860c-ee38e1a23b77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their siege of the Al-Jalda and Deir Baha neighborhoods for a fifth consecutive day, raiding and damaging homes, restricting movement, and obstructing aid deliveries. Since Friday, 619 families have been affected, approximately 3,971 Palestinians forcibly displaced, and 85 arrested.
* Israeli forces also dispersed a protest against the siege with tear gas, causing several people to suffer from tear gas inhalation, and stormed al-Ahli Hospital, firing tear gas at its entrance and courtyard and seizing vehicles from its parking lot.
* **Ramallah and Al-Bireh:** Israeli settlers, protected by Israeli forces, [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/2b69cafd-f539-44af-86f2-df4504d14e89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinian olive harvesters and foreign solidarity activists in Beit Ur Al-Tahta, beating them and firing tear gas and live ammunition.
* In Deir Jarir, two Palestinians were injured in a settler attack. Settlers also established a new outpost with two mobile homes north of Al-Bireh.
* **Nablus:** A Palestinian man was [shot](https://substack.com/redirect/4d21bedd-3900-4161-8b87-df0b14e1572d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the foot near the Huwwara military checkpoint, where Israeli forces obstructed Palestinian Red Crescent medics from reaching him.
* In Burqa, settlers beat a 50-year-old Palestinian man, leaving him with injuries requiring hospitalization. Settlers also detained a Nablus municipal crew repairing a road and seized its equipment.
* **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [forcibly evacuated](https://substack.com/redirect/27a370b1-489d-4224-8031-21336c17eb8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two Palestinian families from their homes in Faroun, converting both houses into military barracks and ordering the families not to return until Wednesday morning.
* **Jericho:** Israeli authorities detained, questioned, and [denied entry](https://substack.com/redirect/1a172bc5-bafc-4a8a-acbb-f63a7e1deb91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a 23-member international delegation through the Karama crossing, preventing them from attending a Birzeit University conference on Global South solidarity and resistance to imperialism.
* **UN commission finds Israel continuing genocide in Gaza despite ceasefire, committing crimes against humanity in West Bank:** Israel continues to commit genocidal acts in Gaza even after the "so-called ceasefire agreement," with the intent to destroy Palestinians "in whole or in part," according to a new [report](https://substack.com/redirect/aef2e6a9-f396-495b-96e0-661c9fd62a23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry.
* The commission also found that Israel has committed war crimes and crimes against humanity, including extermination, persecution, torture, rape, and other forms of sexual violence, across the occupied Palestinian territory.
* In Gaza, Israeli authorities and forces continue to intentionally kill and inflict serious bodily and mental harm on Palestinians despite the October 2025 ceasefire. Israel's expanding territorial control also continues to endanger Palestinians approaching or crossing the Yellow Line.
* In the occupied West Bank, Israeli military operations and settler violence form part of a widespread, systematic and coordinated attack on Palestinians, the report said. Israeli military operations since January 2025 caused the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with 34,176 still displaced as of August 2026.
* Israeli forces also deliberately killed and injured Palestinian children in Gaza and the West Bank, the report found.
* **Netanyahu 's Likud prepares election fraud claims as paid teams monitor Palestinian voters: **Israel's ruling Likud party [deployed](https://substack.com/redirect/9f388b86-894f-49f2-966a-646d02d3398b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) paid teams outside polling stations in Palestinian towns inside Israel to collect footage and testimony that could be used to challenge the results of Tuesday's Knesset election if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc appears headed for defeat, according to a report published by Haaretz.
* The operation, estimated to cost millions of shekels, operates separately from official election monitors and is reportedly approaching coverage of nearly every polling station in Palestinian communities. Information gathered by the teams will be sent to a dedicated "election fraud operations room," while party officials have discussed launching a campaign claiming the election was "stolen" or "rigged" if Netanyahu loses.
* Netanyahu called on Likud supporters to turn out in force on Tuesday. "The future of our Jewish state is at stake: a strong right-wing government or a left-wing government supported by the Arab parties," he [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/abcfcb66-1a2b-4877-a4dc-e20098c415c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a post on X.

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah says Egypt 's pledge of military support for Saudi amounts to a "declaration of war": **Yemen's Ansarallah movement said Egypt's decision to authorize defensive military support for Saudi Arabia against Ansarallah attacks amounts to a "declaration of war" on Yemen, according to AFP.
* "It is truly remarkable that while these parties are supposedly pursuing peace in the region, Egypt and its parliament announce their support for what they call the defense of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," said Mohammed Al-Houthi, a member of Ansarallah's Supreme Political Council. "In doing so, Egypt is declaring war on the Republic of Yemen."
* **Ansarallah claims strike on Saudi oil refinery, military aircraft:** Ansarallah's armed forces [said](https://substack.com/redirect/c069be6b-912f-4af8-8335-cab2c9a1db35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) they struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile, claiming a direct hit that caused massive fires at the facility.
* The group also claimed to have targeted two military transport aircraft with ballistic missiles, one at Najran Airport and another at King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, saying both strikes successfully hit their targets.
* The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by Ansarallah toward Riyadh, the Saudi capital.
* Separately, Ansarallah claimed its forces repelled an attempted advance by Saudi-backed forces from the southern direction of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The group said it targeted troop concentrations with ballistic missiles and heavy weapons, killing and wounding large numbers of fighters and destroying several military vehicles.

# Lebanon
* **Israel shells towns across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire:**
* **Hasbaya:** Israeli forces [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/f6711bb6-7f95-4963-af74-8a1ae9c22057?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four artillery shells into Wadi Shebaa on Tuesday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported.
* **Marjeyoun:** Forces [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/16caac7d-534b-4dee-b157-a3d8511c3b4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a demolition near the cemetery in Khiam, accompanied by heavy machine-gun fire.
* **Tyre (Sour):** Israeli forces shelled the towns of Mansouri and Majdal Zoun.

# U.S. News
* **FTC orders Anthropic executives to testify in consumer-harm probe:** The Federal Trade Commission sent testimony demands to Anthropic and other unnamed AI companies as part of a consumer-harm probe, Axios [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/869e3c45-67f7-49b1-84b8-62e44a52df12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday. The escalation of the probe, which has also involved OpenAI, came the same day that Anthropic began pitching investors on one of the largest IPOs ever. Anthropic said in its S-1 filing that the investigation could bring significant costs to the company, and force changes to its models and.
* **DOJ charges Comey with leaking information:** Federal prosecutors [charged](https://substack.com/redirect/a7d4b792-411e-40ff-9070-a4f607d64e1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the former FBI director **James Comey** with transmitting national defense information and conspiracy, alleging that he "directed staff to speak" with the New York Times reporter **Charlie Savage** about an October 2016 news article. Comey's lawyers said the charges are time-barred because the 10-year limit expired without an indictment. Comey cannot be tried without an indictment or waiver. In response to Monday's announcement, he said, "I'm still innocent."
* Separately, a judge ruled Monday that Comey's daughter **Maurene Comey** was unlawfully fired from the Justice Department and ordered her reinstated.
* **DOJ orders Washington state to set aside ballots from 400+ supposed noncitizens:** The Justice Department****[ordered](https://substack.com/redirect/7ce7fdbe-a858-4d11-b98e-f993215f61c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Washington's secretary of state to set aside the ballots of more than 400 voters that the DOJ claims are "noncitizens." The DOJ's demand came with a 24-hour deadline. The office of the Washington Secretary of State said it is reviewing voting records, though the top agency official, **Steve Hobbs,** said that the timing, a week before midterms, is "no doubt intended to cast unfounded suspicion on the results."
* **Court rejects DOJ attempt to cast doubt on 20,000 California ballots:** A federal appeals court [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/cbf34e9d-e45f-4288-8762-4b2580ec5d7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that the DOJ cannot order California to sequester the ballots of 20,000 voters that the Trump administration says are "likely noncitizens." A panel of the Ninth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 2-1 against the DOJ's attempt to cast doubt on the ballots. The Trump-appointed judge **Mark Bennett** said that the Constitution gives California power over its voter rolls, and the Biden-appointed judge **Gabriel Sanchez** questioned the reliability of the DOJ's claim that 20,000 California voters could be "noncitizens." Voting is already underway in California, where every voter receives a mail-in ballot.
* **AP: ICE detained mentally ill man for almost a year despite records showing he was born in the U.S.:** ICE arrested **Phillip James** , a U.S. citizen, in January and has held him in detention ever since, according to an Associated Press [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/220fff20-aca7-4a07-9751-1111219f8678?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). James, who has paranoid schizophrenia, said that he was born in Jamaica, but a Florida birth certificate and a 1988 paternity case show that he was born in Orange County, Florida. He was also issued a U.S. passport. An immigration judge ordered James' deportation to Jamaica in April, though Jamaica said that it has no record of his being born there. His lawyers have petitioned federal judge **Damon** **Leichty** for his release.
* **FT: Donald Trump Jr. attended hunting trip with Russian oligarch close to Putin:** In August, **Donald Trump Jr.** went on a hunting trip in western Mongolia with the Russian oligarch **Umar Kremlev** , who has personal ties to Russian President **Vladimir Putin** , the Financial Times [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/69b4bfa7-70fa-4ae4-a6a7-7259034a48a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). A spokesperson told the FT that Kremlev and Trump Jr. have a strictly "personal relationship, not a business relationship." The expose follows a ProPublica [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf11a00-d713-44a9-85f7-a1589304330e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Kremlev spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on Trump Jr.'s ritzy Bahamas wedding. President Donald Trump said his son repaid Kremlev for the wedding funding.

# Other International News
* **Egyptian court orders closure of leading news outlet Mada Masr, detains editor:** An Egyptian court continued its attack on Mada Masr on Tuesday, convicting its editor-in-chief and co-founder Lina Attalah on the charge of running an unlicensed website. The court ordered the closure of the publication, took Attalah into custody, and fined her 3 million Egyptian pounds (about $50,000). Mada Masr is one of the country's last remaining independent news organizations. The rulings followed a sham one-day trial in which Attalah's legal requests to present documents and call witnesses were rejected, after which the court appointed an unknown attorney in place of her existing legal team. The outlet, which was founded in 2013, has repeatedly applied for licensure, but has received no response from Egyptian authorities. The Committee to Protect Journalists condemned the ruling, calling Mada Masr "a vital source of critical reporting" and the decision a "devastating blow to press freedom in Egypt."
* **Bolsonaro effectively concedes defeat in Brazil, lacking Trump intervention and fearing prosecution:** Flavio Bolsonaro [dropped](https://substack.com/redirect/d8c76a1d-929f-470c-8c70-64277600946f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his demand that Sunday's presidential election be annulled minutes after Trump said he "didn't take sides" in the race. Bolsonaro said he would sue President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva for abuse of incumbency, a routine challenge that his camp does not expect to succeed. A Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his passport amid a probe of possible corruption and money laundering. Bolsonaro denies wrongdoing. One of his advisers said that he conceded the election, in part, out of fear of imprisonment.
* **Drone strike in RSF-held territory kills at least 21, injures 40; western nations warn of famine:** A drone strike [hit](https://substack.com/redirect/6103d251-1306-440b-9e02-de65117fb3d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a market in Ayala, the Rapid Support Forces' (RSF) de facto capital, on Monday, killing at least 21 people and injuring at least 40 others. Sudanese Armed Forces regularly strike the city. Separately, RSF drone strikes hit a Khartoum transformer station on Tuesday.
* On Monday, the United States, the European Union, and 30 other countries [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/78f23fe7-7e84-4e2e-9ee3-2e89c8c6169e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Sudan is undergoing an "alarming deterioration in its food security." The countries called for "urgent action" to avoid famine.
* **Congo exceeds 10,000 Ebola cases:** The Democratic Republic of the Congo [surpassed](https://substack.com/redirect/9c6ab3af-8b4a-4b71-a6ca-3cf756790c6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 10,000 confirmed Ebola cases, according to government data published on Tuesday. Almost 4,900 of these cases resulted in death. The Congo's Ebola epidemic is the fastest-growing and deadliest outbreak in the country's history, and the second-largest Ebola outbreak recorded. Around 80% of new cases have occurred outside the chains of transmission that health authorities are monitoring. Several treatment centers are reportedly overwhelmed by infections. At least half of people who died from Ebola were never admitted to a health facility.
* **89,000+ people evacuated in eastern India ahead of Cyclone Arnab:** Indian authorities [evacuated](https://substack.com/redirect/d9a2c641-d0c8-4109-854e-de14744c0a36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 89,000 people from coastal areas in the eastern state of Andhra Pradesh, ahead of a "very severe" storm, Cyclone Arnab, that is expected to hit the region by Wednesday morning. More than 12 million people live along the storm's projected path. Authorities in the area have opened over 2,000 shelters, secured 30,000 fishing boats, and deployed over 1,000 medical teams. The neighboring state of Odisha plans to evacuate almost 50,000 people.
* **Attacks in Ethiopia kill at least 60 Orthodox Christians:** Two attacks in the Oromia region of Ethiopia have killed at least 60 Orthodox Christians over the last week, the Ethiopian Orthodox Church [said](https://substack.com/redirect/0271487f-59da-47bf-b521-8112e172f719?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Fourteen people were killed in Merti district on October 20, and 46 were killed in Shirka district on October 24. More than 20 people were seriously wounded in the attacks, and 20 homes were burned. A regional spokesperson accused the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA) of the attacks, without presenting evidence. The OLA couldn't be reached, and its leader has previously denied targeting civilians. The OLA belongs to an alliance formed in September to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed from power.
* **Jordan strikes Syria in response to Karak church attack, killing at least seven:** Jordan [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/8f3ab41f-ba45-43b0-adc5-8c85ee8d2f1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four sites in the Syrian cities of Deraa and Suweyda on Monday, killing seven people, according to the Syrian Civil Defence. Among the victims was a family of five, including three children. Jordan's military said the strikes came in response to last week's attack on a church in Karak. A Jordanian spokesman acknowledged some civilian deaths, but said that the strikes killed 20 Islamic State fighters.
* **Romania accuses Russia-backed actors of sabotaging weapons factory:** The Romanian Intelligence Service [said](https://substack.com/redirect/bbd947d8-b71c-430d-b7b9-4572f4dc2279?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that it had "uncovered" a Russia-backed network responsible for setting fire to a state-owned weapons factory in September. The attack was "part of a wider campaign of sabotage operations coordinated" by Russia against arms makers and other military and industrial targets, the agency said. Romanian authorities have identified three suspects. Russia has not commented on the case.
* **Colombia to withdraw from Hague Group coalition over stance on Israel:** Colombia formally requested to leave The Hague Group, a group of states aiming to hold Israel accountable for war crimes, a Colombian government spokesperson [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/075ace9d-5235-45b4-bd8f-3fba5b394b6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday. The spokesperson said that the group aims "to isolate and attack Israel." The Hague Group was formed in 2025 by nine countries of the Global South to support the rulings of the International Criminal Court and the International Court of Justice. It has sought to curtail weapons sales to Israel.
