This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iran hails emerging regional order without foreign intervention after Tehran meeting: Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey Iranian leaders in Tehran on Monday for talks on regional security and escalating tensions, with Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei declaring that "a new atmosphere is emerging in the region." Rezaei said the sides held "very good" talks and agreed that West Asia's security should be managed by regional states, without foreign intervention. The "results of the Iranian nation's resistance" are becoming more tangible "day by day," he said. The four countries said they would "continue the dialogue," and officials called it the first in an expected series of meetings, though no date has been set. Oman says excluding Iran from Gulf security has been a fundamental mistake: Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi decades of Gulf security arrangements built around excluding Iran and relying on foreign military powers, calling for a new regional security framework that includes Tehran. "Perhaps the most damaging of the priorities imposed on the region from the outside has been the requirement that Iran be excluded," he said during a lecture at Cambridge University. This, he said, created an unstable system based on the "entirely false perception" of fundamental antagonism between Iran and Arab Gulf states. "There is no such fundamental antagonism," he said, adding that any security architecture excluding Iran is "inherently unstable" and "structurally unsound." He also said that Oman and Iran had developed the outline of a temporary arrangement to restore navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, but said implementation would require compromises by both Tehran and Washington. He maintained that a U.S.-Iran nuclear agreement had been within reach before the U.S.-Israeli war began on February 28, an assessment Oman continues to stand by. Iran says oil tanker caught fire after striking naval mines east of Hormuz: An oil tanker caught fire after striking naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy said Tuesday. The vessel had entered a prohibited area with its tracking systems switched off, according to Iranian state media. Separately, Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority announced that all vessels belonging to South Korean shipping company Sinokor will face legal action beginning November 1, accusing the company of repeatedly violating passage regulations in the Strait. The authority, established by Tehran to manage vessel transit requests through the waterway, said Sinokor had recorded the highest number of crossing violations over the past three months and that "appropriate actions" had already been taken against at least seven of its vessels. UK charges two British men in Iran-linked investigation at U.S. bomber base: Two British nationals were under the UK's National Security Act following an investigation into a September security incident at RAF Fairford, a British airbase used by U.S. bombers. One man is charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, while another is charged with entering a prohibited site for a purpose prejudicial to the UK. RAF Fairford has been used by the U.S. to deploy bombers to the Middle East, including after Britain authorized its use for strikes against Iran. The U.S. withdrew its bombers following the incident. British counterterrorism police said they believe several recent incidents were directed by the Iranian state. Iran has denied involvement. Palestine Six-year-old girl dies of wounds from Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis: A six-year-old Palestinian girl Tuesday morning from wounds sustained after being shot by Israeli forces in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis, southern Gaza, WAFA reported. Over the past 24 hours, six Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks and 32 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, is now 74,561 killed, with 175,759 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,565 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,640, while 845 bodies have been recovered. Israel bars delegates from Birzeit University conference as settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank: Hebron: Israeli forces their siege of the Al-Jalda and Deir Baha neighborhoods for a fifth consecutive day, raiding and damaging homes, restricting movement, and obstructing aid deliveries. Since Friday, 619 families have been affected, approximately 3,971 Palestinians forcibly displaced, and 85 arrested. Israeli forces also dispersed a protest against the siege with tear gas, causing several people to suffer from tear gas inhalation, and stormed al-Ahli Hospital, firing tear gas at its entrance and courtyard and seizing vehicles from its parking lot. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: Israeli settlers, protected by Israeli forces, Palestinian olive harvesters and foreign solidarity activists in Beit Ur Al-Tahta, beating them and firing tear gas and live ammunition. In Deir Jarir, two Palestinians were injured in a settler attack. Settlers also established a new outpost with two mobile homes north of Al-Bireh. Nablus: A Palestinian man was in the foot near the Huwwara military checkpoint, where Israeli forces obstructed Palestinian Red Crescent medics from reaching him. In Burqa, settlers beat a 50-year-old Palestinian man, leaving him with injuries requiring hospitalization. Settlers also detained a Nablus municipal crew repairing a road and seized its equipment. Tulkarm: Israeli forces two Palestinian families from their homes in Faroun, converting both houses into military barracks and ordering the families not to return until Wednesday morning. Jericho: Israeli authorities detained, questioned, and to a 23-member international delegation through the Karama crossing, preventing them from attending a Birzeit University conference on Global South solidarity and resistance to imperialism. UN commission finds Israel continuing genocide in Gaza despite ceasefire, committing crimes against humanity in West Bank: Israel continues to commit genocidal acts in Gaza even after the "so-called ceasefire agreement," with the intent to destroy Palestinians "in whole or in part," according to a new by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry. The commission also found that Israel has committed war crimes and crimes against humanity, including extermination, persecution, torture, rape, and other forms of sexual violence, across the occupied Palestinian territory. In Gaza, Israeli authorities and forces continue to intentionally kill and inflict serious bodily and mental harm on Palestinians despite the October 2025 ceasefire. Israel's expanding territorial control also continues to endanger Palestinians approaching or crossing the Yellow Line. In the occupied West Bank, Israeli military operations and settler violence form part of a widespread, systematic and coordinated attack on Palestinians, the report said. Israeli military operations since January 2025 caused the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with 34,176 still displaced as of August 2026. Israeli forces also deliberately killed and injured Palestinian children in Gaza and the West Bank, the report found. Netanyahu 's Likud prepares election fraud claims as paid teams monitor Palestinian voters: Israel's ruling Likud party paid teams outside polling stations in Palestinian towns inside Israel to collect footage and testimony that could be used to challenge the results of Tuesday's Knesset election if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc appears headed for defeat, according to a report published by Haaretz. The operation, estimated to cost millions of shekels, operates separately from official election monitors and is reportedly approaching coverage of nearly every polling station in Palestinian communities. Information gathered by the teams will be sent to a dedicated "election fraud operations room," while party officials have discussed launching a campaign claiming the election was "stolen" or "rigged" if Netanyahu loses. Netanyahu called on Likud supporters to turn out in force on Tuesday. "The future of our Jewish state is at stake: a strong right-wing government or a left-wing government supported by the Arab parties," he in a post on X. Yemen Ansarallah says Egypt 's pledge of military support for Saudi amounts to a "declaration of war": Yemen's Ansarallah movement said Egypt's decision to authorize defensive military support for Saudi Arabia against Ansarallah attacks amounts to a "declaration of war" on Yemen, according to AFP. "It is truly remarkable that while these parties are supposedly pursuing peace in the region, Egypt and its parliament announce their support for what they call the defense of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," said Mohammed Al-Houthi, a member of Ansarallah's Supreme Political Council. "In doing so, Egypt is declaring war on the Republic of Yemen." Ansarallah claims strike on Saudi oil refinery, military aircraft: Ansarallah's armed forces they struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile, claiming a direct hit that caused massive fires at the facility. The group also claimed to have targeted two military transport aircraft with ballistic missiles, one at Najran Airport and another at King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, saying both strikes successfully hit their targets. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by Ansarallah toward Riyadh, the Saudi capital. Separately, Ansarallah claimed its forces repelled an attempted advance by Saudi-backed forces from the southern direction of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The group said it targeted troop concentrations with ballistic missiles and heavy weapons, killing and wounding large numbers of fighters and destroying several military vehicles. Lebanon Israel shells towns across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire: Hasbaya: Israeli forces four artillery shells into Wadi Shebaa on Tuesday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Marjeyoun: Forces a demolition near the cemetery in Khiam, accompanied by heavy machine-gun fire. Tyre (Sour): Israeli forces shelled the towns of Mansouri and Majdal Zoun. U.S. News FTC orders Anthropic executives to testify in consumer-harm probe: The Federal Trade Commission sent testimony demands to Anthropic and other unnamed AI companies as part of a consumer-harm probe, Axios on Monday. The escalation of the probe, which has also involved OpenAI, came the same day that Anthropic began pitching investors on one of the largest IPOs ever. Anthropic said in its S-1 filing that the investigation could bring significant costs to the company, and force changes to its models and. DOJ charges Comey with leaking information: Federal prosecutors the former FBI director James Comey with transmitting national defense information and conspiracy, alleging that he "directed staff to speak" with the New York Times reporter Charlie Savage about an October 2016 news article. Comey's lawyers said the charges are time-barred because the 10-year limit expired without an indictment. Comey cannot be tried without an indictment or waiver. In response to Monday's announcement, he said, "I'm still innocent." Separately, a judge ruled Monday that Comey's daughter Maurene Comey was unlawfully fired from the Justice Department and ordered her reinstated. DOJ orders Washington state to set aside ballots from 400+ supposed noncitizens: The Justice Department Washington's secretary of state to set aside the ballots of more than 400 voters that the DOJ claims are "noncitizens." The DOJ's demand came with a 24-hour deadline. The office of the Washington Secretary of State said it is reviewing voting records, though the top agency official, Steve Hobbs, said that the timing, a week before midterms, is "no doubt intended to cast unfounded suspicion on the results." Court rejects DOJ attempt to cast doubt on 20,000 California ballots: A federal appeals court on Monday that the DOJ cannot order California to sequester the ballots of 20,000 voters that the Trump administration says are "likely noncitizens." A panel of the Ninth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 2-1 against the DOJ's attempt to cast doubt on the ballots. The Trump-appointed judge Mark Bennett said that the Constitution gives California power over its voter rolls, and the Biden-appointed judge Gabriel Sanchez questioned the reliability of the DOJ's claim that 20,000 California voters could be "noncitizens." Voting is already underway in California, where every voter receives a mail-in ballot. AP: ICE detained mentally ill man for almost a year despite records showing he was born in the U.S.: ICE arrested Phillip James , a U.S. citizen, in January and has held him in detention ever since, according to an Associated Press . James, who has paranoid schizophrenia, said that he was born in Jamaica, but a Florida birth certificate and a 1988 paternity case show that he was born in Orange County, Florida. He was also issued a U.S. passport. An immigration judge ordered James' deportation to Jamaica in April, though Jamaica said that it has no record of his being born there. His lawyers have petitioned federal judge Damon Leichty for his release. FT: Donald Trump Jr. attended hunting trip with Russian oligarch close to Putin: In August, Donald Trump Jr. went on a hunting trip in western Mongolia with the Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev , who has personal ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin , the Financial Times . A spokesperson told the FT that Kremlev and Trump Jr. have a strictly "personal relationship, not a business relationship." The expose follows a ProPublica that Kremlev spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on Trump Jr.'s ritzy Bahamas wedding. President Donald Trump said his son repaid Kremlev for the wedding funding. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Egyptian court orders closure of leading news outlet Mada Masr, detains editor: An Egyptian court continued its attack on Mada Masr on Tuesday, convicting its editor-in-chief and co-founder Lina Attalah on the charge of running an unlicensed website. The court ordered the closure of the publication, took Attalah into custody, and fined her 3 million Egyptian pounds (about $50,000). Mada Masr is one of the country's last remaining independent news organizations. The rulings followed a sham one-day trial in which Attalah's legal requests to present documents and call witnesses were rejected, after which the court appointed an unknown attorney in place of her existing legal team. The outlet, which was founded in 2013, has repeatedly applied for licensure, but has received no response from Egyptian authorities. The Committee to Protect Journalists condemned the ruling, calling Mada Masr "a vital source of critical reporting" and the decision a "devastating blow to press freedom in Egypt." Bolsonaro effectively concedes defeat in Brazil, lacking Trump intervention and fearing prosecution: Flavio Bolsonaro his demand that Sunday's presidential election be annulled minutes after Trump said he "didn't take sides" in the race. Bolsonaro said he would sue President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva for abuse of incumbency, a routine challenge that his camp does not expect to succeed. A Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his passport amid a probe of possible corruption and money laundering. Bolsonaro denies wrongdoing. One of his advisers said that he conceded the election, in part, out of fear of imprisonment. Drone strike in RSF-held territory kills at least 21, injures 40; western nations warn of famine: A drone strike a market in Ayala, the Rapid Support Forces' (RSF) de facto capital, on Monday, killing at least 21 people and injuring at least 40 others. Sudanese Armed Forces regularly strike the city. Separately, RSF drone strikes hit a Khartoum transformer station on Tuesday. On Monday, the United States, the European Union, and 30 other countries that Sudan is undergoing an "alarming deterioration in its food security." The countries called for "urgent action" to avoid famine. Congo exceeds 10,000 Ebola cases: The Democratic Republic of the Congo 10,000 confirmed Ebola cases, according to government data published on Tuesday. Almost 4,900 of these cases resulted in death. The Congo's Ebola epidemic is the fastest-growing and deadliest outbreak in the country's history, and the second-largest Ebola outbreak recorded. Around 80% of new cases have occurred outside the chains of transmission that health authorities are monitoring. Several treatment centers are reportedly overwhelmed by infections. At least half of people who died from Ebola were never admitted to a health facility. 89,000+ people evacuated in eastern India ahead of Cyclone Arnab: Indian authorities at least 89,000 people from coastal areas in the eastern state of Andhra Pradesh, ahead of a "very severe" storm, Cyclone Arnab, that is expected to hit the region by Wednesday morning. More than 12 million people live along the storm's projected path. Authorities in the area have opened over 2,000 shelters, secured 30,000 fishing boats, and deployed over 1,000 medical teams. The neighboring state of Odisha plans to evacuate almost 50,000 people. Attacks in Ethiopia kill at least 60 Orthodox Christians: Two attacks in the Oromia region of Ethiopia have killed at least 60 Orthodox Christians over the last week, the Ethiopian Orthodox Church . Fourteen people were killed in Merti district on October 20, and 46 were killed in Shirka district on October 24. More than 20 people were seriously wounded in the attacks, and 20 homes were burned. A regional spokesperson accused the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA) of the attacks, without presenting evidence. The OLA couldn't be reached, and its leader has previously denied targeting civilians. The OLA belongs to an alliance formed in September to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed from power. Jordan strikes Syria in response to Karak church attack, killing at least seven: Jordan four sites in the Syrian cities of Deraa and Suweyda on Monday, killing seven people, according to the Syrian Civil Defence. Among the victims was a family of five, including three children. Jordan's military said the strikes came in response to last week's attack on a church in Karak. A Jordanian spokesman acknowledged some civilian deaths, but said that the strikes killed 20 Islamic State fighters. Romania accuses Russia-backed actors of sabotaging weapons factory: The Romanian Intelligence Service that it had "uncovered" a Russia-backed network responsible for setting fire to a state-owned weapons factory in September. The attack was "part of a wider campaign of sabotage operations coordinated" by Russia against arms makers and other military and industrial targets, the agency said. Romanian authorities have identified three suspects. Russia has not commented on the case. Colombia to withdraw from Hague Group coalition over stance on Israel: Colombia formally requested to leave The Hague Group, a group of states aiming to hold Israel accountable for war crimes, a Colombian government spokesperson on Tuesday. The spokesperson said that the group aims "to isolate and attack Israel." The Hague Group was formed in 2025 by nine countries of the Global South to support the rulings of the International Criminal Court and the International Court of Justice. Peter -We're entering the final stretch of this election, and one thing is becoming increasingly clear: **races across Nevada are incredibly close,** and the difference between victory and defeat could come down to just a handful of votes.**That's why I'm asking you to do three things today.**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

## 1\. MAKE A PLAN TO VOTE — AND DON'T WAIT UNTIL ELECTION DAY!
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
If you haven't voted yet, please make a plan to do so NOW.
Four years ago, historically bad weather hit Nevada on Election Day, keeping voters away from the polls and contributing to heartbreaking losses in races Republicans should have won.
We cannot afford to let that happen again.
There is simply too much at stake in this election.** From the Governor's Office to the State Treasurer's Office to Congress and the two ballot initiatives, the decisions Nevada voters make over the next eight days will shape our state's future for years to come.**
Early voting runs through Friday, October 30. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3.
**Please, don't leave your vote to chance. Vote early. Return your mail ballot. Make sure your voice is heard.**
---
| |

## **2\. HELP MAKE SURE YOUR FRIENDS AND FAMILY VOTE, TOO.**
---
| |
Once you've voted, don't stop there!

Governors' races are arguably the most overlooked and understated battlegrounds of this entire election cycle.

Hey folks,
Pete Hegseth has a rebellion on his hands.
Military review boards were reportedly given a clear mission: push transgender service members out. Instead, the people actually serving alongside them are looking at their records, looking at their service, and voting to keep them. That tells you everything.
* [**00:01:23**] Military review boards are reportedly defying Hegseth's push to remove transgender troops, voting to retain service members in nine out of 12 cases discussed here.
* [**00:03:23**] I get into why this matters beyond one policy fight: Hegseth can give speeches and perform toughness for MAGA, but the people underneath him increasingly seem unwilling to follow his lead.
* [**00:06:18**] We hear the story of Marine Staff Sergeant Damian Contreras, whose fellow service members reportedly looked past the instructions, examined his record, and decided a good Marine deserves to remain a Marine.
* [**00:09:57**] The story gets even more disturbing as we discuss reporting that the Pentagon is searching medical records to identify transgender troops who remain in uniform.
* [**00:12:24**] I end with the part that makes me furious: patriotism means loving this country's people, especially the people willing to put their bodies on the line to defend the rest of us.

This isn't really a story about Pete Hegseth's culture-war bullshit. It's about service, loyalty, leadership, and what patriotism actually demands from us. These Americans volunteered to serve their country, and now their own government is targeting them because of who they are. Meanwhile, the people who actually served beside them are standing up. **If you value independent media that refuses to look away when powerful people target vulnerable Americans, help me keep fighting.**

| | | Oregon votes by mail, every voter and every election. So last month's Supreme Court ruling hit close to home. Trump's rules would have forced states to adopt new ballot envelopes and upload absentee voters' names and barcodes to an online platform that didn't exist yet. Election officials warned that where they couldn't comply in time, mail voting would essentially be canceled. The Court blocked the rules for the 2026 midterms. **_That was a win, but it wasn't the end._** **In September, Trump told supporters to "try and cheat like hell, like they do." His Justice Department is trying to force states to turn over their voter rolls. His Homeland Security secretary wouldn't rule out sending ICE agents to polling places, and only later said they'd be sent just for "specific threats" or warrants.** Utah's Republican lieutenant governor put it this way: "The threats that we're getting now are mostly from our own government." **She called Washington's handling of elections "dangerous, disruptive and in bad faith."** When Republicans who run elections say that out loud, no one can dismiss it as partisan noise. **[I'm going to keep fighting these schemes in public and telling it straight to voters. clean_body: | | | = | | | Oregon votes by mail, every voter and every election. So last month's Supreme Court ruling hit close to home. Trump's rules would have forced states to adopt new ballot envelopes and upload absentee voters' names and barcodes to an online platform that didn't exist yet. Election officials warned that where they couldn't comply in time, mail voting would essentially be canceled. The Court blocked the rules for the 2026 midterms. That was a win, but it wasn't the end. In September, Trump told supporters to "try and cheat like hell, like they do." His Justice Department is trying to force states to turn over their voter rolls. His Homeland Security secretary wouldn't rule out sending ICE agents to polling places, and only later said they'd be sent just for "specific threats" or warrants. Utah's Republican lieutenant governor put it this way: "The threats that we're getting now are mostly from our own government." She called Washington's handling of elections "dangerous, disruptive and in bad faith." subject: On the ground in California

body:
It’s Get-Out-The-Vote season, and I’m traveling to key districts to help canvass for our candidates.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261027-1&t=1&akid=4196%2E587540%2EOiLR9Z)
Peter,
In this final sprint towards Election Day, I’m excited that I get to be on the ground, speaking to voters about critical races across the country. Last week, I had the opportunity to get-out-the-vote up and down California.
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261027_1_ca.l0o4cQ&refcode=em20261027-4196&amount=5&t=2&akid=4196%2E587540%2EOiLR9Z)
In Sacramento, I knocked doors with Mai Vang and an energizing group of volunteers who are ready for progressive change. I also had the privilege of attending the No Kings rally and speaking at a Youth Roundtable.
Mai’s opponent has been in Congress for twenty years, traded over $37 million during that time, and is relying on corporate money (and her personal wealth) to fund her campaign. **Mai is ready to be the true progressive voice we need in Congress.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261027_1_ca.l0o4cQ&refcode=em20261027-4196&amount=5&t=3&akid=4196%2E587540%2EOiLR9Z)
Down in the Central Valley, the energy was electric as I talked to voters in CA-22 with Randy Villegas. Randy is running in one of the most critical red-to-blue Congressional races in the country, and the latest polls show him pulling ahead of his MAGA opponent, Rep. David Valadao.
The enthusiasm I experienced canvassing for Randy made it clear: Voters are tired of the increasing costs at the gas pump, the grocery store, and the cuts to their healthcare. **They are ready to elect Randy Villegas.**
These races are incredibly close and will decide the balance of power in Congress. And our candidates are up against opponents who have streams of corporate and even personal money flowing in. **Just like Leaders We Deserve, Mai and Randy don’t take a dime of corporate PAC money — their campaigns are fueled by grassroots supporters like you chipping in what you can, when you can.**
Leaders We Deserve exists to help elect the leaders who will bring the change we want to see, and Randy and Mai are critical to making that vision a reality.
**[Can you rush $5 to help Leaders We Deserve get Mai, Randy, and all of our candidates across the finish line next week?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261027_1_ca.l0o4cQ&refcode=em20261027-4196&amount=5&t=4&akid=4196%2E587540%2EOiLR9Z)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

Peter, Even Republicans have started asking the obvious question about why their own party keeps crying fraud. In a recent interview with MSNOW, **Congressman Thomas Massie** asked why Republicans complain about rigged elections when the last major election handed the GOP resounding majorities under the very same rules.
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt87ca0SDQiJzPwLxh_6q8C0Ow2O6ztXJ_TUvyn-Vhn52NATJ1VkPj2JS2nmf34vmlJEWv0P8Ewh-xYuopjY66dnJ7qhOFx5wtcHHVY4F4dF5Co-Z7W3wXPPK7YrswVNnYEDcavXyHnnzfh2d4gVJU4mEZZDymUkNAlkxbTTFwUofBjqa5oTS6k4Lhg8rJZLdzGDSV8eLMulDP7IzpcgXhs6qja4uqkLh6OIJfBGa72-5J0HPTzFN721lrLKzvqM0-c4YY3JOA-rLpEu_ElI9ttv0KWlo5uizFQtwu6KR9aUANcJTgaeUt311r5W2daytPxg/4v8/ofDgKIa5T7OBFHVnxNVp5g/h1/h001.8B8drAfvXO63OH55-bz8NivjOkNhGeDLVvF6wXSAGaA)
---
[ **Answer the Big Lie with a Bigger Win.** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt87ca0SDQiJzPwLxh_6q8C0Ow2O6ztXJ_TUvyn-Vhn52NlEwQaOCfKNM7ri1xe8zLYwhnLjiOahB7ABBGPAr5V0e4B9preit9UgQJopqu0YoSpW-AVDd66Q5wiz4uEbru8TdSsHMRG3ERfNvEHcAoorTLgACNESBf6S8fGoK8Y8O6HXLPTW_A60n-Ga4rGRtRzPJOCdMEO_cKg1_MWK6kvitedfeLWg_N_kRkbCuA4zI3Q2DhivTm5uqI0vMUinS0NpKlMAXkoWxisjvAaJnAdSO2jIABsbv9_mZM3aZVt__EhTj7_wNc2P7mqGr27BP91Q/4v8/ofDgKIa5T7OBFHVnxNVp5g/h2/h001.NlhwYUFBRM7ob3IG86UntCmbvGceeToAkbN17xb1S9o)
---
The truth is this cynical tactic has a dangerous precedent we all remember.
Trump spent the back half of 2020 telling anyone who would listen that the election was getting stolen from him.
That lie grew until it filled a mob with enough rage to storm the U.S. Capitol on January 6th in the greatest armed assault on our democracy since the Civil War. That violent insurrection led to the deaths of nine people including five Capitol police officers – four of whom died by suicide because of what they experienced that day.
Six years later, the same seeds are being planted.
Trump keeps floating a “national security emergency” around the midterms.
DHS has threatened to put ICE agents near polling places to chase the made-up problem of “illegals voting.”
And in Alaska, Republican lawyers stand ready to sue instead of certifying a Senate loss over a ranked choice system their own voters approved.
Each of these stories teaches people to assume that any election these extremists lose must have been tampered with.
---
[ **Beat the Big Lie 2.0. Flip TX-03.** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt87ca0SDQiJzPwLxh_6q8C0Ow2O6ztXJ_TUvyn-Vhn52Nurn3wMfcjcDNU7cc79u59EF3SGH4R8QPDRuACEemcGf26Sda6Ps8ijPBIcJIt6Ye6KQL3dq-0BqI0X0jxiQ5t1cTEmFddTjJhckKKDfe3zjhdzyj2nctmEATrl8Me1JnM1XRlG29BV_PGgmD88NB99e4sR1XKA0HhXi2nA-j3CZ5OVb_hVr3UaDokPpbgt54fdYrJIJGdBfw8x7MxfJn1Bzgp7_q1EVcDic0f0pUiAay464kGTGBPibRtZHdpwTKzPdAknPdtfnJsQRLHWskhQ/4v8/ofDgKIa5T7OBFHVnxNVp5g/h3/h001.qHVmPXOYpHtI6-qtm7y0pKf0NYkqEZ4nbrD4zsJAVOA)
---
Now, I won’t fearmonger and tell you this administration is about to cancel the midterms or toss your ballot in the trash.
Our laws are stronger than that, and so are the Texans running our elections.
Experts went through all 130-plus powers a national emergency unlocks.
None let a president take over an election.
None let him change the voting rules, cancel the vote, or throw out a state’s results.
But we also know better than to bet the farm on this president respecting the rule of law.
So here’s what we do about it.
We organize on two fronts.
On one, we trust the law and the courts to hold the line.
On the other, we run up a score so lopsided that no conspiracy theory can touch it.
[Chip in and help us put this race out of reach.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt87ca0SDQiJzPwLxh_6q8C0Ow2O6ztXJ_TUvyn-Vhn52NN1k2QcB-KTSNpBDj8uaet9LFfsFjazjA3Cl9quoldFE0rbxsFk___8XIOGDSq-_FE-cEEIk7BKjk9XcaqW7XlSzc41lvtZmPHBB9u2IT7dHknyaHOZDQXJtjBFAy_Gm9NVB7uqeSDeUTfCP4Df2MwrDI_Ftzc3LG9lAW8LQbkBvl_hWcXPd36q_RhsxMrvNju0pUCbZAVeM3xfxcGa5YvnNhrZDkwRJkVZ81BK_R3JIWyyObUGPUKNTeO3dMc97IsyGNZR4MwnK3aRZCYwdPIg/4v8/ofDgKIa5T7OBFHVnxNVp5g/h4/h001.XrFh1rytFtSMdv9MfHNy_mOIE0kCN6HMyTJ2PXIrh5Y)
The good news is Texans are already doing it. Lines have wrapped around the block all week for early voting. People tracking the early vote report that a quarter of Collin County has voted with 8 days still to go.
My family and I joined them this weekend.

clean_body: A level-headed look at what Trump can and cannot do to this election. | | Peter, Even Republicans have started asking the obvious question about why their own party keeps crying fraud. In a recent interview with MSNOW, Congressman Thomas Massie asked why Republicans complain about rigged elections when the last major election handed the GOP resounding majorities under the very same rules. | The truth is this cynical tactic has a dangerous precedent we all remember. Trump spent the back half of 2020 telling anyone who would listen that the election was getting stolen from him. That lie grew until it filled a mob with enough rage to storm the U.S. Capitol on January 6th in the greatest armed assault on our democracy since the Civil War. That violent insurrection led to the deaths of nine people including five Capitol police officers – four of whom died by suicide because of what they experienced that day. Six years later, the same seeds are being planted. Trump keeps floating a “national security emergency” around the midterms. DHS has threatened to put ICE agents near polling places to chase the made-up problem of “illegals voting.” And in Alaska, Republican lawyers stand ready to sue instead of certifying a Senate loss over a ranked choice system their own voters approved. Each of these stories teaches people to assume that any election these extremists lose must have been tampered with. Now, I won’t fearmonger and tell you this administration is about to cancel the midterms or toss your ballot in the trash. Our laws are stronger than that, and so are the Texans running our elections. Experts went through all 130-plus powers a national emergency unlocks. None let a president take over an election. None let him change the voting rules, cancel the vote, or throw out a state’s results. But we also know better than to bet the farm on this president respecting the rule of law. So here’s what we do about it. We organize on two fronts. On one, we trust the law and the courts to hold the line. On the other, we run up a score so lopsided that no conspiracy theory can touch it. The good news is Texans are already doing it. Lines have wrapped around the block all week for early voting. People tracking the early vote report that a quarter of Collin County has voted with 8 days still to go. My family and I joined them this weekend. | Folks were proud and fired up to be there. Millions of Texans are refusing to be bullied out of faith in their own democracy, and I could not be prouder to stand with them. name: GIFFORDS
subject: [ADD YOUR NAME] Demand gun safety legislation from the next Congress
disclaimer_text: paid for by the gun lobby, and by people like Elon Musk who would rather enrich themselves than keep our kids safe
body:
Gun violence is the leading cause of death for kids and teens in America.
#

Friend -
Gun violence is the leading cause of death for kids and teens in America.
More than drug overdoses. More than car accidents.
**Gun violence is number one.**
This horrifying statistic shows the stronghold that the gun violence epidemic has on our nation. How many more children must die before Congress takes action? We must do better for our children, for our future.
That’s why, in advance of November’s elections, we’re starting a petition to call on Congress to pass transformative legislation to keep our kids safe from gun violence.
[**Will you click here to add your name today and demand that our elected officials take action to protect our children from gun violence?**](https://go.giffords.org/signup/Kids_Petition_sv_/?source=em261027-1-b&refcode2=11974.3935704.Hedng6&akid=11974%2E3935704%2EHedng6)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://go.giffords.org/signup/Kids_Petition_sv_//?source=em261027-1-b&refcode2=11974.3935704.Hedng6&akid=11974%2E3935704%2EHedng6)**
To protect our kids, we must pass safe storage laws to ensure gun owners properly store their firearms so that their children cannot access them and accidentally injure themselves or others.
We must pass background checks on all gun sales at the federal level to make sure we’re keeping guns out of the wrong hands, like people convicted of violent felonies.
We must pass extreme risk protection order (aka “red flag”) laws to prevent school shootings before they occur. Our kids should be able to attend school without fear of being a victim of another mass shooting.
We’re working overtime to elect a Congress that will take action. But we’re up against members of Congress bought and paid for by the gun lobby, and by people like Elon Musk who would rather enrich themselves than keep our kids safe.
**We cannot be silent. Children are dying and we must do something.**
[**Please team, sign on today to demand that Congress has the courage to protect our children by prioritizing gun safety legislation.**](https://go.giffords.org/signup/Kids_Petition_sv_/?source=em261027-1-b&refcode2=11974.3935704.Hedng6&akid=11974%2E3935704%2EHedng6)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://go.giffords.org/signup/Kids_Petition_sv_//?source=em261027-1-b&refcode2=11974.3935704.Hedng6&akid=11974%2E3935704%2EHedng6)**
Thank you for using your voice. If we work together, we can be a better, safer nation.
\- The team at Giffords

We try to send only the most important information and opportunities to participate via email, but click [here](https://go.giffords.org/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=2&akid=11974%2E3935704%2EHedng6) if you'd like to unsubscribe. Giffords PAC was started to support elected officials who step up to fight the gun violence epidemic. Thank you for standing with Gabby and the Giffords team.

**The debate posed a clear choice for voters:****Change course – or accept more of the same?**
On Friday, October 23, Nancy and Congressman Smucker met at the Country Barn in Lancaster for the election season’s only debate.
The event hosted 200 attendees, while local watch parties and supporters nationwide also tuned in. Thousands have since viewed WGAL’s livestream, now available on its [YouTube channel](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFVLUdi8i151w50enNxxZ/QEg0fhvoTkzd).
Although the candidates agreed on a few points during the hour-long debate, their remarks revealed sharply different views of how PA-11 should be represented.
Smucker emphasized his record in Washington, while Nancy stressed the need for change to better serve the district. Here are a few highlights:

* **On affordability:**

Smucker “hoped” that prices would come down after the wars in Iran and Ukraine ended. He believes the economy is working “...other than the price of fuel...,” and stated several times that manufacturing is “resurging” in the U.S.
_FACT CHECK_ : Manufacturing activity has strengthened in 2026, with growth in areas including transportation equipment, defense-related production, and computer and electronic products. However, the recovery remains uneven: output is rising modestly, while factory employment has stayed near recent levels rather than reflecting a broad resurgence.1
See for yourself. The chart below illustrates the number of manufacturing jobs in Lancaster through 2025:
---
---
Nancy said the economy has worsened this year and that affordability is the top concern raised at her town halls, emphasizing that prices have risen sharply since February because of the war in Iran.

* **On making healthcare more accessible and affordable:**

Smucker proposed greater competition, direct payments to providers, and Health Savings Accounts to lower costs and expand access. Nancy advocated universal healthcare, beginning with a Medicare-style program for all children – and committed to working across the aisle to make it happen.

* **On the historic $40 trillion national debt** : Smucker talked in platitudes about the issues regarding the national debt – blaming both Republicans and Democrats. He pointed to the “Big Beautiful Bill” and the decisions that were made as part of it to address it.

Nancy argued that the country has a spending-priorities problem. She said the “Big Beautiful Bill,” shepherded through Congress by Smucker, increased the national debt by making tax cuts for the ultra-wealthy permanent and eliminating 3,000 IRS positions responsible for high-value audits.

* **On immigration** : Nancy called for commonsense immigration reform. She noted that the United States has spent $155 billion on immigration enforcement since 2025, resulting in U.S. citizens being detained or killed and nonviolent immigrants being deported. She also criticized ending temporary protected status for 1 million people, 80% of whom who were employed and contributing $36 billion annually to the gross domestic product. Nancy proposed a legal pathway to citizenship and reminded the audience that immigration violations are civil offenses that should be handled in civil court.

Smucker praised Trump for the immigration efforts and noted the drop in crime and drug deaths due to the deportation of these illegal immigrants. He then agreed with Nancy that if someone is in the country, playing by the rules, paying taxes and contributing to society, they should be able to stay.
_FACT CHECK_ : Since 2023, violent crime is down 16 percent across Pennsylvania – including a 39 percent drop in homicides, a 45 percent decrease in robberies involving a firearm, and a 25 percent reduction in firearm assaults. This is due to Governor Shapiro’s administration which has distributed $1 billion through 6,700 grants targeted to lowering violent crime.2

* **On foreign diplomacy** : Smucker said he supports Ukraine and opposes Putin’s invasion. Although he questioned Trump’s recent actions, he said he “...doesn’t want to tie Trump’s hands...” in negotiations to end the war with Iran, citing concerns about Iran obtaining a nuclear weapon. He also added, “...I think you will see gas prices come down, and hopefully that happens soon...”

Nancy then challenged Smucker directly with her stance:“...We were in an agreement with Iran regarding nuclear weapons. In 2018, President Trump withdrew from that agreement and that began the weakening of the oversight in Iran. In April, you said this war will be over soon, just like you are saying today. That was eight months ago. We have seen the impact of this conflict in Iran: 21 dead soldiers, more than 800 wounded, over ten thousand civilians who have been killed and thousands injured.
The President, you say, is within his powers to wage war, but the Constitution, again, assigns that responsibility to Congress. You voted five times against a war powers resolution act, not holding Donald Trump in check. If you cannot or will not do your duty as a congressman to control our military and to control our executive office, then you should step aside and let someone who will uphold the constitution do that job.”

In a statement over the weekend, Nancy said, “I'm grateful for the opportunity to share my positions and vision for our future during this week's debate. I hope the debate made the differences between Lloyd Smucker and me clear, not just in our positions, but in who we believe we should be fighting for.”

The chart below illustrates the number of manufacturing jobs in Lancaster through 2025: Nancy said the economy has worsened this year and that affordability is the top concern raised at her town halls, emphasizing that prices have risen sharply since February because of the war in Iran. On making healthcare more accessible and affordable: Smucker proposed greater competition, direct payments to providers, and Health Savings Accounts to lower costs and expand access. Nancy advocated universal healthcare, beginning with a Medicare-style program for all children – and committed to working across the aisle to make it happen. On the historic $40 trillion national debt : Smucker talked in platitudes about the issues regarding the national debt – blaming both Republicans and Democrats. He pointed to the “Big Beautiful Bill” and the decisions that were made as part of it to address it. Nancy argued that the country has a spending-priorities problem. She said the “Big Beautiful Bill,” shepherded through Congress by Smucker, increased the national debt by making tax cuts for the ultra-wealthy permanent and eliminating 3,000 IRS positions responsible for high-value audits. On immigration : Nancy called for commonsense immigration reform. She noted that the United States has spent $155 billion on immigration enforcement since 2025, resulting in U.S. citizens being detained or killed and nonviolent immigrants being deported. She also criticized ending temporary protected status for 1 million people, 80% of whom who were employed and contributing $36 billion annually to the gross domestic product. Nancy proposed a legal pathway to citizenship and reminded the audience that immigration violations are civil offenses that should be handled in civil court. Smucker praised Trump for the immigration efforts and noted the drop in crime and drug deaths due to the deportation of these illegal immigrants. He then agreed with Nancy that if someone is in the country, playing by the rules, paying taxes and contributing to society, they should be able to stay. FACT CHECK : Since 2023, violent crime is down 16 percent across Pennsylvania – including a 39 percent drop in homicides, a 45 percent decrease in robberies involving a firearm, and a 25 percent reduction in firearm assaults. This is due to Governor Shapiro’s administration which has distributed $1 billion through 6,700 grants targeted to lowering violent crime.2 On foreign diplomacy : Smucker said he supports Ukraine and opposes Putin’s invasion. Although he questioned Trump’s recent actions, he said he “...doesn’t want to tie Trump’s hands...” in negotiations to end the war with Iran, citing concerns about Iran obtaining a nuclear weapon. He also added, “...I think you will see gas prices come down, and hopefully that happens soon...” Nancy then challenged Smucker directly with her stance:“...We were in an agreement with Iran regarding nuclear weapons. In 2018, President Trump withdrew from that agreement and that began the weakening of the oversight in Iran. In April, you said this war will be over soon, just like you are saying today. That was eight months ago. We have seen the impact of this conflict in Iran: 21 dead soldiers, more than 800 wounded, over ten thousand civilians who have been killed and thousands injured. The President, you say, is within his powers to wage war, but the Constitution, again, assigns that responsibility to Congress. You voted five times against a war powers resolution act, not holding Donald Trump in check. If you cannot or will not do your duty as a congressman to control our military and to control our executive office, then you should step aside and let someone who will uphold the constitution do that job.” In a statement over the weekend, Nancy said, “I'm grateful for the opportunity to share my positions and vision for our future during this week's debate. I hope the debate made the differences between Lloyd Smucker and me clear, not just in our positions, but in who we believe we should be fighting for.” 1. 2. | ✉️ Enjoying These Campaign Updates? | Peter, earlier this week I told you about the memo from Trump's allies laying out how Congress could refuse to seat democratic socialists who win their elections.
No one writes up a plan like that about a movement they think is going away. [ Bill ]Bill Nye

Hi Peter,
it’s Bill Nye.

I’ll get right to it: I’m reaching out to ask for your help electing Dr.
Abdul El-Sayed to the U.S. Senate from Michigan.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261027-2-ak.czGLtF&amount=10&refcode=em20261027-3762&t=1004&akid=3770%2E251025%2EUvDEUo ]Before I say more, can you chip in $10 or any amount
right now so that Abdul can reach as many voters as possible in Michigan
before Election Day?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261027-2-ak.czGLtF&amount=10&refcode=em20261027-3762&t=1005&akid=3770%2E251025%2EUvDEUo ]Donate $10 ››

Peter, I’d like
you to consider the following:

Pollution is chemistry. When a refinery releases sulfur dioxide, the gas
drifts into nearby neighborhoods and ends up in the lungs of the people
who live closest to it.

That part is just basic science, and we can’t change the laws of nature.
Whether the company gets permission to release more of those toxins,
unrestricted, is where politics comes into play.

Abdul understands that connection through his studies in medical school.
He sees how something like scrapping limits on toxic “forever chemicals”
in our drinking water can lead to those chemicals end up being consumed by
Michigan families.

A lot of folks in Washington seem to have forgotten that science is
written into the Constitution. Article I, Section 8, Clause 8 gives
Congress the job “to promote the Progress of Science.” Standing up for
science isn’t partisan. It’s about as American as it gets.

That’s why I’m with Abdul.

Abdul trained as a doctor and an epidemiologist. He follows the evidence.
He takes on corporate polluters. And he sticks to his values by not taking
a dime from corporate PACs. No polluter can buy Abdul.

Abdul is looking out for the future.

But that future won’t build itself. It starts with electing people who
believe in it, including Abdul.

Election Day is in 7 days. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261027-2-ak.czGLtF&amount=10&refcode=em20261027-3762&t=1006&akid=3770%2E251025%2EUvDEUo ]Will you chip in $10 or any
amount so that Michigan sends someone to the Senate who respects science
and can’t be bought?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261027-2-ak.czGLtF&amount=10&refcode=em20261027-3762&t=1025&akid=3770%2E251025%2EUvDEUo ]Donate $10 ››

Onward,

Bill Nye

She could’ve died. Texas said there was nothing they could do. | | | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/142295060/656454619/2141984067?sourceid=1151697&utm_campaign=27emcge-1005aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=stories&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMzVhZTQwOC0yNGQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJkNTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QlYL-BtdU1eUWiQ82XqrlGAGb7GxFrKGkqAtpIzpflw=&emci=d05ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&emdi=d35ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&ceid=954237) | | [DONATE](https://click.everyaction.com/k/142295061/656454620/2141984067?sourceid=1151697&utm_campaign=27emcge-1005aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=stories&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMzVhZTQwOC0yNGQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJkNTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QlYL-BtdU1eUWiQ82XqrlGAGb7GxFrKGkqAtpIzpflw=&emci=d05ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&emdi=d35ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&ceid=954237)
---
| Peter—

When Kelsie Norris-De La Cruz walked into the emergency room, she was in pain, cramping, and bleeding.

She was experiencing an ectopic pregnancy, a life-threatening condition that demands immediate care. An emergency room doctor even said Kelsie's fallopian tube could rupture.

**But Kelsie lives in Texas, under one of the most extreme abortion bans in the country. She was shown the door. No care. No transfer to another hospital.** [Kelsie was on her own.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/142295062/656454621/-172117553?sourceid=1151697&utm_campaign=27emcge-1005aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=stories&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMzVhZTQwOC0yNGQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJkNTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QlYL-BtdU1eUWiQ82XqrlGAGb7GxFrKGkqAtpIzpflw=&emci=d05ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&emdi=d35ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&ceid=954237) | [Read Kelsie's Story](https://click.everyaction.com/k/142295063/656454622/-172117553?sourceid=1151697&utm_campaign=27emcge-1005aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=stories&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMzVhZTQwOC0yNGQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJkNTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QlYL-BtdU1eUWiQ82XqrlGAGb7GxFrKGkqAtpIzpflw=&emci=d05ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&emdi=d35ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&ceid=954237)
---
Kelsie sought a second opinion from another OB-GYN, who diagnosed the ectopic pregnancy and performed emergency surgery to save her life. But the delay cost Kelsie a fallopian tube — and compromised her future fertility.

["Despite the fact that my life was clearly in danger, the hospital told me that they could not help me," Kelsie said. "If I was made to wait any longer, it's very likely I would have died."](https://click.everyaction.com/k/142295064/656454623/-172117553?sourceid=1151697&utm_campaign=27emcge-1005aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=stories&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMzVhZTQwOC0yNGQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJkNTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QlYL-BtdU1eUWiQ82XqrlGAGb7GxFrKGkqAtpIzpflw=&emci=d05ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&emdi=d35ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&ceid=954237)

The Center for Reproductive Rights represented Kelsie and filed federal complaints against two hospitals for violating EMTALA, the law requiring hospitals to provide emergency care. Kelsie put it plainly: "Texas state officials can't keep ignoring us. We can't let them."

**The Center for Reproductive Rights is proud to fight for brave women like Kelsie. Their stories deserve to be heard -- and those responsible deserve to be held accountable.**

[Read Kelsie's story and join the call to end abortion bans for good.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/142295065/656454624/-172117553?sourceid=1151697&utm_campaign=27emcge-1005aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=stories&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMzVhZTQwOC0yNGQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJkNTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QlYL-BtdU1eUWiQ82XqrlGAGb7GxFrKGkqAtpIzpflw=&emci=d05ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&emdi=d35ae408-24d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&ceid=954237)

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

In a district this size, that’s a margin you could lose on any given block in Westminster or Fullerton. **22 days** That’s how long we waited after Election Day before the AP called our race. name: Sean Feucht
subject: #TestimonyTuesday: 102 years old—and the last one to leave worship
body:
The highlight of my night and one of the best moments this year!| | |
---
| |
---
_Even in old age they will still produce fruit; they will remain vital and green._ —Psalm 92:14 Could there be a more appropriate verse for today's #TestimonyTuesday? At 102 years old, Betty Brown came to worship with us in Los Angeles. And when we were packing up at 10:15 that night, she was the last one out the door. I watched her come down to the altar with her walker, lifting her hands to Jesus. After a lifetime of faith, her hunger for His presence was still burning. Betty told me she’d been part of the Aimee Semple McPherson revival in Los Angeles. When I asked if she believed God would do it again, she didn’t hesitate: **“Absolutely..._in a greater way_.”** Seeing Betty worship was one of the highlights of my year. Her faith challenged me—and I believe her story will encourage you today. **Watch today’s #TestimonyTuesday below!**

name: VoteVets.org
subject: Trump’s arch will cast a shadow over John F. Kennedy’s tomb and more than 50,000 graves at Arlington National Cemetery.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
#
Peter —
When CBS News asked Donald Trump who his 250-foot Arc de Trump was being built for, he pointed at himself and said, “Me.”
We’re seeing that firsthand.
Using VoteVets’ analysis, _The Washington Post_ just released an article that shows the Arc de Trump will cast a shadow directly over John F. Kennedy’s tomb and the eternal flame — along with more than 50,000 graves across Arlington National Cemetery.
[](https://act.votevets.org/signup/Arc_Shadow_su_em/?source=em261027-1-180&refcode2=35762.3013755.ZVTE2Y&akid=35762%2E3013755%2EZVTE2Y)
Most of these graves belong to service members and Veterans the public will never hear of. Every one of them earned that ground the way President Kennedy did — by serving.
The man raising the arch did not. He took five draft deferments during the Vietnam War and never served a day in his life. Now, he wants to put up a monument to himself that would leave a permanent shadow over those who did serve.
**The National Capital Planning Commission is expected to take up final approval on November 5.** It must wait. The government owes the dead of Arlington and their families a true study on the effects of the Arc de Trump before the irreversible vote.
[**Please add your name to our petition demanding the National Capital Planning Commission delay the final vote on the Arc de Trump.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/Arc_Shadow_su_em/?source=em261027-1-180&refcode2=35762.3013755.ZVTE2Y&akid=35762%2E3013755%2EZVTE2Y)

---
No one gets to make this decision twice. We must raise hell while there’s still time.
Thank you,
VoteVets

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: In February, they didn’t think I had a chance →
body:
The Houston Chronicle recently endorsed me, and what they wrote about Abbott says everything you need to know.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**The Houston Chronicle, the paper of record in Texas’s largest city, recently endorsed me for governor.**
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261027_4_chron.49st5p&refcode=em20261027-2562&t=1&akid=2562%2E299639%2EAIgYA2)
I want to be honest about something: when I met with their editorial board in February, they didn’t think Greg Abbott had much to worry about. They said so right in the endorsement. I was a state rep with little name recognition outside Austin, running against a three-term incumbent with a $106 million war chest.
Eight months later, they’ve endorsed me.
**But what stuck with me most in their endorsement wasn’t what they said about me. It was what they said about how much Greg Abbott has changed.**
Texans first met Abbott in the ’90s, when he ran for judge in Houston. Back then he came across as a moderate, Bush-era Republican who even picked up Democratic votes. Three decades later, the Chronicle calls him a “relentless, hardcore MAGA standard-bearer.”
Look at what he’s done with the power he’s been given:
* Texas currently has the most people without health insurance, the most people being disconnected from their electricity, and the most bankruptcies of any state.
* He stripped Texas communities of local control.
* And he’s taken care of the billionaires who fund him:
* A $1 million check from a gas tycoon whose company cashed in during Winter Storm Uri.
* $12 million from a Pennsylvania billionaire while Abbott pushed vouchers that drain money from rural public schools.
* A billion dollars a year in tax breaks for data centers.

**That’s the question at the heart of this race: which Texans does Greg Abbott serve? It isn’t working families.**
When I left that editorial board meeting, I told them I think people are tired of fighting. Tired of a government that works for the powerful instead of for them. **After 30 years of one-party rule, Texans are ready for change.**
Early voting is going on _right now_. Abbott still has _millions_ to spend, and he’ll use every dollar to keep things exactly the way they are.
If you’ve been waiting to make your first contribution, let this be the moment. [**Will you chip in $15 to help us bring our message to every Texan throughout early voting?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20261027_4_chron.25Tj2Z&refcode=em20261027-2562&t=3&akid=2562%2E299639%2EAIgYA2)

Thank you,
Gina

Texans first met Abbott in the ’90s, when he ran for judge in Houston. Back then he came across as a moderate, Bush-era Republican who even picked up Democratic votes. Three decades later, the Chronicle calls him a “relentless, hardcore MAGA standard-bearer.” Look at what he’s done with the power he’s been given: Texas currently has the most people without health insurance, the most people being disconnected from their electricity, and the most bankruptcies of any state. He stripped Texas communities of local control. And he’s taken care of the billionaires who fund him: A $1 million check from a gas tycoon whose company cashed in during Winter Storm Uri. $12 million from a Pennsylvania billionaire while Abbott pushed vouchers that drain money from rural public schools. A billion dollars a year in tax breaks for data centers. That’s the question at the heart of this race: which Texans does Greg Abbott serve? It isn’t working families. When I left that editorial board meeting, I told them I think people are tired of fighting. Tired of a government that works for the powerful instead of for them. After 30 years of one-party rule, Texans are ready for change. Early voting is going on right now. Abbott still has millions to spend, and he’ll use every dollar to keep things exactly the way they are. If you’ve been waiting to make your first contribution, let this be the moment. Peter,
**Election Day is ONE WEEK from today** , and now it all comes down to who shows up.
If you haven’t voted yet, **early voting runs through THIS FRIDAY, October 30.** Make your plan, then remind your family, friends, and neighbors. **EVERY single vote matters.**
The contrast in this election couldn’t be clearer:
* **We want to cut taxes and lower costs.** Democrats want higher taxes on middle-class families.
* **We want to secure the border.** They want open borders and mass amnesty.
* **We want to back the blue.** They’ve embraced an agenda that calls for abolishing the police.
* **We want to increase Texas oil and gas jobs.** They want to phase out fossil fuels and drive up your energy bills.
* **We want to protect girls’ sports and the Second Amendment.** They push a radical woke agenda.

This election is [**common sense vs. crazy**](https://us.list-manage.com/YuMPkYJ2xLz?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)**.**[**Vote early**](https://us.list-manage.com/Hz0zYvqc8Qc?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)**** and remind all your friends!

When I launched this campaign over a year ago, I knew I was in for a tough fight. The political class said I couldn't do it, we were going up against a 3-term incumbent with over $100 million sitting in the bank.
Now a year later, we've effectively tied this race against Greg Abbott, despite being outspent 10-to-1 and facing hundreds of millions of dollars in attack ads.
But I didn't launch this campaign to make history or splashy headlines. I launched it because I believed in a better future for the people of Texas, and I was ready to do whatever it took to fight for it.
That's why I've dedicated this past year of my life to driving across our beautiful state, meeting with people bearing the brunt of the failed leadership in Texas.
Texans deserve a government that listens to them, works for them, and puts their needs first.
My plan as your next governor of Texas is simple: I want to put money back in your pocket, save our neighborhood schools, and end the political corruption running rampant in our state.
_**There 's One Fight this November -- will Texas be a state that is by and for the people, or is this the billionaires' world and we just live here?**_
We're in the final seven days before the last votes are cast, and I'm still fighting to make Texas a place where hardworking people can achieve American Dream.
For me, that has always meant that if you work hard, you should not just survive -- you should thrive in this country and in Texas.
It means that if you work a full-time job, you should be able to own your own home, pay your bills, have kids and send them to a good school in the neighborhood, take a vacation once in a while, and retire with dignity.
But under Greg Abbott, Texas has the highest uninsured rate in the entire country. People are being priced out of their homes because of high property taxes and outrageous electricity bills. And communities are being forced to compete with data centers for their drinking water.
_This election is an opportunity to change that._
**With just one week remaining, we have to go all in on securing a better vision for the future of Texas.** I'm still on the ground on my _One Fight_ tour, mobilizing voters and getting our message out to undecided Texans. And I am asking you to please cast your ballot for me and encourage your friends and family to do the same.
Texans deserve a seat at the table -- no more being pushed to the back of the line while the rich and powerful get ahead.
That's our fight. That's the work we have left to do in these final seven days. Thank you for being a supporter and someone committed to getting me elected. I'm ready to deliver for Texans, but need your help in this final push to get me across the finish line.

I'm still fighting, and I need you in it with me.

body:

It’s
Hillary Clinton.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/24018?t=1002&akid=2090%2E181023%2EGK1Rla ]Today, I am asking you to join me in supporting my friend, Jocelyn
Benson, to be Michigan’s next governor.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/24018?t=1003&akid=2090%2E181023%2EGK1Rla ]Donate →

It’s easy to feel exhausted and hopeless lately. Every day, we hear
another upsetting soundbite and read another disgusting headline about
Donald Trump’s backwards priorities.

That’s by design. Donald Trump wants us to
get distracted by his appalling stunts and lose hope that anything will
ever change. His success relies on it.

But
anxiety is not a strategy.

In just 7 days, we have a chance to stand up and fight back, and it’s
going to take everyone to put a check on Trumpism and protect our
neighbors.

Democratic governors are the last line of defense against Trump’s unhinged
agenda.

Cutting the costs of your rent, healthcare, groceries – it’s all on the
line. But truth be told, this election isn’t just about what happens
today. It’s about who is at the helm of one of the most important
battleground states in 2028.

In 2028, Donald Trump is going to have a hand-picked candidate for
President on the ballot, and we’ve seen the meltdown that happens when he
loses.

When he tries to overturn election results yet again, we need someone
leading Michigan who is prepared to protect the will of the people and
fight back against anyone who tries to undermine our democracy. That’s
Jocelyn Benson.

Jocelyn has the experience this moment calls for. She has spent her career
fighting to protect Michigan’s elections. When Donald Trump’s lies led to
armed protesters on her front lawn, she stood by the people of Michigan.
When Donald Trump tried to threaten her to overturn private voting data,
she took him to court and won.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/24018?t=1004&akid=2090%2E181023%2EGK1Rla ]Take it from me, going head-to-head with Donald Trump is no easy feat,
but it is what Michigan needs from their governor. That’s why I’m proud to
stand with my friend Jocelyn Benson. Will you please join me and make a
donation today to help her win on November 3rd and keep fighting for
Michiganders?

# [NBA just handed Kalshi and Polymarket the keys to official betting](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The NBA designated Kalshi and Polymarket **[as preferred prediction-market exchanges Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/28c777cc-a742-4740-86b3-9ba09ef528dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and signed a memorandum of understanding **[with the CFTC focused on integrity protections and data sharing.](https://substack.com/redirect/585a0a6a-03a2-4891-8cdb-e3f3e1d7e46f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Preferred status:** The exchanges receive rights to NBA intellectual property, marketing, licensing, and official data from Sportradar to operate and settle authorized markets.
* **Integrity framework:** Agreements limit permissible contracts, bar league and team personnel from trading NBA event contracts, and require information sharing on suspicious activity.
* **CFTC memorandum:** The[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/f67ab217-9637-429f-aa8b-3e035a391c95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[deal with the agency](https://substack.com/redirect/f67ab217-9637-429f-aa8b-3e035a391c95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** aims to maintain integrity of both the league and event-contract markets through coordinated monitoring.
* **League statement:** NBA media partnerships head Scott Kaufman-Ross said protecting game integrity is the top priority and that the partnerships create new fan-engagement opportunities.

# [Broadcom locks $63 billion to fund Anthropic's AI chip spree](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Broadcom **[arranged a $63 billion special-purpose vehicle](https://substack.com/redirect/1a858b73-7626-47ff-968f-0386535fa685?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with **[Bank of America, Blackstone, Citigroup, and Morgan Stanley](https://substack.com/redirect/8bdcda49-0eb3-4dd6-ab09-849b82cf86be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to buy its chips and lease them to Anthropic, with residual-value support from the chipmaker.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **SPV structure:** The vehicle will purchase Broadcom silicon and networking gear and lease it to the Claude developer, with deliveries expected to begin in 2027.
* **Bank roles:** Bank of America, Citigroup, and Morgan Stanley are arranging first-lien financing; Blackstone is providing the committed second-lien portion.
* **CEO involvement:** Broadcom CEO Hock Tan intervened after nearly two months of negotiations to **[help seal the package.](https://substack.com/redirect/58fd6edc-1d57-45f8-8bce-7e151f5e847f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Context:** The deal ranks among the largest AI-infrastructure financings and sits alongside Anthropic's broader compute commitments disclosed in its S-1.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/467557e5-69f9-45b9-b826-31fa62992863?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
# [Surgery Partners stock jumps 46% on $5.7 billion HealthSpan takeover](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Surgery Partners **[shares surged](https://substack.com/redirect/5f442d19-cb5b-4114-ab24-9a267443c29a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of Bon Secours Mercy Health, **[agreed to take the company private](https://substack.com/redirect/e6d73500-9bb7-4c50-a6b5-ae203d7c944c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in a deal valued at about $5.7 billion including debt.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Deal terms:** Remaining shareholders will receive $23.50 per share, a roughly 49% premium to the prior close; Bain Capital retains its 39% stake.
* **Scale:** The combination adds more than 200 sites across 30 states and about 5,000 affiliated physicians to Bon Secours' network.
* **Timing:** The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027 and ends a multi-year strategic review.
* **Share reaction:** Surgery Partners rose as much as 48% on the announcement as outpatient surgery remains a focus for health systems.

# [SoftBank's Son plans $50 billion AI bet in Malaysia](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said SoftBank's Masayoshi Son **[selected locations in Sarawak](https://substack.com/redirect/e9fc2b66-6f05-47f7-9adc-118ad7e88b13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and peninsular Malaysia for **[$50 billion in AI,](https://substack.com/redirect/ab49c305-f7fb-43b0-9b2a-5db4a3e540e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/ab49c305-f7fb-43b0-9b2a-5db4a3e540e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)technology, and data-center investment.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Locations:** Son identified Kuching in Sarawak and areas on the peninsula during a video conference with Anwar.
* **Scope:** The outlay covers AI, new technology, and data centers and ranks among the largest planned investments in the region.
* **Prior framework:** SoftBank earlier signed a framework agreement in Kuching with Grab and state energy company PETROS to explore AI infrastructure.
* **Confirmation:** SoftBank has not publicly confirmed the $50 billion figure; Anwar disclosed the plan in a speech in Melaka.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/467557e5-69f9-45b9-b826-31fa62992863?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
# [Kalshi lands exclusive S&P Dow Jones deal for index contracts](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Kalshi **[became a preferred prediction-market platform](https://substack.com/redirect/118db513-731f-42f3-b28f-f11df4352272?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for S&P Dow Jones Indices, gaining rights to list event contracts **[tied to benchmarks such as the S&P 500](https://substack.com/redirect/4fdf68e9-9fac-4c29-a2cb-4c226834c4f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4fdf68e9-9fac-4c29-a2cb-4c226834c4f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)that will settle against official index values.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Preferred status:** Kalshi is licensed as a preferred platform for S&P DJI index-linked event contracts; S&P DJI becomes a preferred provider for indices built from Kalshi data.
* **Settlement:** Forthcoming contracts will settle against official S&P DJI index values, the same reference standard used in professional markets.
* **New indices:** The collaboration opens the door for indices on economics, politics, and sports constructed from Kalshi event-contract data.
* **Statements:** Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour called S&P DJI the gold standard for benchmarks; S&P DJI CEO Cathy Clay said the deal extends its role into one of the fastest-growing market categories.

* * *
# [Celestica surges after AI boom and $40 billion 2027 target](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Celestica shares[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/a45cbfa2-70b1-4a03-96b5-3e3e5e1246fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[jumped after the company reported third-quarter revenue of $5.83 billion,](https://substack.com/redirect/a45cbfa2-70b1-4a03-96b5-3e3e5e1246fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** up 83% year over year, and raised its outlook **[while targeting $40 billion in revenue for 2027.](https://substack.com/redirect/9b1e7726-0a28-4fb6-a21c-40527cc0581e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Quarterly results:** Adjusted EPS reached $3.30, above the high end of guidance, with adjusted operating margin of 8.5%.
* **Raised outlook:** Full-year 2026 revenue guidance increased to $21 billion from $20.5 billion; adjusted EPS guidance rose to $11.55.
* **2027 target:** Initial outlook calls for $40 billion in revenue, roughly 90% growth, with a 9.0% adjusted operating margin.
* **AI demand:** Management cited strong hyperscaler and frontier-lab demand as the driver of accelerating growth.
