# [Whirlpool sinks on guidance cut while Boeing slips on miss](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Whirlpool shares **[fell after the appliance maker cut full-year guidance,](https://substack.com/redirect/5f442d19-cb5b-4114-ab24-9a267443c29a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5f442d19-cb5b-4114-ab24-9a267443c29a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)while **[Boeing declined following an earnings miss](https://substack.com/redirect/7cef4c32-2faa-4a10-8fa3-0447a54bfc36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/7cef4c32-2faa-4a10-8fa3-0447a54bfc36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)as traders sorted through a busy premarket slate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/841c169d-c231-44ac-b685-b4cf75b54fd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Whirlpool cut:** The company reduced its full-year adjusted earnings outlook, sending shares lower in extended trading and the premarket.
* **Boeing miss:** Shares slid after the aerospace company reported a wider-than-expected quarterly core loss.
* **Market backdrop:** The moves occurred as futures pointed higher on softer oil prices and continued interest in the Anthropic filing.

Charlie said it best in the days leading up to President Trump's victory in 2024: _" I don't care about polls. __ __I don 't care about betting markets. __ __I don 't care about vibes. __ _ **_I care about how many ballots are in the box. _**_ __If we turnout, we win. __ _**_Do the work. " _** Do the work... Charlie knew there was no easy route to saving our country. He knew there were no shortcuts to victory. He wore a red band on his wrist every day -- a reminder of what it would take -- that read, _**" Be Better. Work Harder." **_ It wasn't just for motivation. Charlie lived by those four words, and he expected every one of us at Turning Point to live by them too. body:

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,

Here’s what [The Denver Post](https://us.list-manage.com/_dTzYZ8K4pi?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8) said in their endorsement of our campaign: **“Bridges will bring unrivaled enthusiasm to a statewide office that is often overlooked.”**
As I said in my [campaign video](https://us.list-manage.com/4jl61bce0W_?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8), Treasurer is anything but boring.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/18Q8jS7wxTE?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | And it’s not just my attitude they like! The Post also praised my plan to invest Colorado dollars in Colorado.
“Bridges wants to advocate for a small amount of the investment funds the state holds... to be invested in safe and investment income-generating Colorado businesses and projects. **We think that is a great idea.** ”
As I’ve said for two years now, we have billions of dollars parked in Washington and Wall Street. We should put more of that money to work right here at home in housing, infrastructure, and creating good jobs. The Post agrees.

This is the clear opportunity in the Treasurer’s office. Not just managing money, but finding ways to lower the cost of living for Colorado families. I’m grateful to the Denver Post for their endorsement and for recognizing the potential of our approach.
And—of course—if you’re in a place to help us finish this campaign strong, I would appreciate the support.
---

Case File No DRT-ED-PLAYBOOK · Special File · The Cold War Rerun
In 1982, Washington Put a Strategy Against the Soviet Economy in Writing. Forty-Four Years Later, the Same Pressure Points Are Being Tested on China.
Reagan’s team didn’t only build missiles. It went after the Soviet Union’s money, its technology and its energy lifeline. Today the U.S. is choking off China’s access to advanced chips, and Beijing is answering with its grip on rare earths. A truce over those minerals runs out on November 10.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Most people remember the end of the Cold War as a story about walls and summits. But a big part of it was fought on spreadsheets: export licenses, credit lines and energy revenue. Those tools never disappeared. They were just put in a drawer, and now they’re back on the table.
The evidence board
| | What the Record Shows
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the directive.** On November 29, 1982, President Reagan signed National Security Decision Directive 66, which committed the U.S. and its allies to limit the Soviet Union’s access to Western credit and high technology.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the pain point.** When world oil prices collapsed in 1986, the Soviet Union lost an estimated $20 billion a year in revenue, according to estimates cited by PolitiFact. Oil and gas were Moscow’s main source of hard currency.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the new front.** Since October 2022, Washington has restricted China’s access to advanced AI chips and the tools to make them. Beijing answered in October 2025 with sweeping rare-earth export controls, then suspended them until November 10, 2026.
| OUR THEORY
---
The weapons of economic war are the same as before: technology, money and energy. What’s new is the target. China is far bigger and more connected to the world economy than the Soviet Union ever was, so the side effects of this fight will reach investors everywhere.
Connected file
| | Energy Is Still a Weapon
---|---
The Soviet story shows how much power sits in energy. Today, the U.S. is the world’s largest producer of oil and natural gas, and much of the pipeline and storage network that moves it is owned by partnerships that pay investors cash distributions every quarter.
Some income investors are lining these payments up into a calendar.
| | Sponsored by Behind the Markets

I've written a lot about the 3000 county strategy of progressive Democrats. Here is something new for the file.
Elections are decided twice. Once by the voters, and once by whoever decides where the voters live and who pays for the ads. Two stories surfaced this month that are really one story, and both of them end at your ballot box.
**I. The Map**
You've likely heard about the proposed Heartland Visa -- a new visa category to repopulate 1,700 rural counties with foreign workers. The think tank behind it is the Economic Innovation Group, co-founded by Sean Parker, Facebook's founding president. EIG's own words: "In exchange for living in a Heartland Visa community, workers with sufficient earnings will gain permanent residency." A struggling town supplies the address. Washington supplies the immigration pathway. Stay six years, get the green card. Five years after that, citizenship. And a citizen votes.

name: Chad Bianco
subject: Stand With Your Deputies
body:
Call and email all five Supervisors now

| | | | | |
---
| STOP DEFUNDING OUR DEPUTIES $125 million shortfall · Over 600 fewer deputies at risk
---
| |

**A MESSAGE FROM SHERIFF CHAD BIANCO.**

Friends,
The Board of Supervisors’ ad hoc committee is seeking public feedback on creating a new “oversight” committee for the Sheriff’s Department.

**I have serious concerns about this proposal and the political motivations behind it.** Some of the same activists advocating for this committee recently pressured the Board to defund our Sheriff’s Department by **$125 million, threatening more than 600 deputy positions.**
**We already have federal, state, and local oversight.** This committee won’t make you safer. It’s a waste of tax dollars and more political lawfare from Sacramento’s playbook.
---
| | | | | BE RESPECTFUL. BE ASSERTIVE.
MAKE YOUR VOICE HEARD.
---
| |

**Riverside County residents — get vocal today.** Call your Supervisor. Email your Supervisor. Tell them you oppose this committee. Flood the phone lines. Fill their inboxes. Be nice. Be respectful. And be assertive. **While you don’t get a vote on this, you still have influence.**

Every time a new agency, department, or committee is proposed to the public, it sounds like a great idea. But in the end, it’s just another layer of bureaucracy **wasting your hard-earned money,** and most of the time, like in this case, it will be used for political control.
**Share this with your Facebook friends, neighbors, and family.** People need to know what the Board is doing. I cannot stress enough, how vital it is that the board hears from you and not just the activists who want fewer deputies on your streets.
---
| District 1 SUPERVISOR JOSE MEDINA **Phone:** (951) 955-1010
**Email:** district1@rivco.org
---
District 2 SUPERVISOR KAREN SPIEGEL **Phone:** (951) 955-1020
**Email:** district2@rivco.org
District 3 SUPERVISOR CHUCK WASHINGTON **Phone:** (951) 955-1030
**Email:** D3Email@rivco.org
District 4 SUPERVISOR V. MANUEL PEREZ **Phone:** (951) 955-1040
**Email:** district4@rivco.org
District 5 SUPERVISOR YXSTIAN GUTIERREZ **Phone:** (951) 955-1050
**Email:** district5@rivco.org
|
---
| **Not sure which district you’re in?** [Find your Supervisor here](https://us.list-manage.com/erLAABem8F4?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d) — then call and email yours.
---
| | SUBMIT YOUR FEEDBACK TO THE BOARD
---
Use the County’s official form to tell the Board where you stand on this ad hoc “oversight” committee.
[SUBMIT FEEDBACK](https://us.list-manage.com/L6yKwNxtVrx?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
Or copy this link:
[https://rivco.gov/ad-hoc-committee-feedback-form-0](https://us.list-manage.com/3_B1MYti7k_?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
---
| |

I’ve had your back. Now I’m asking you to have mine. **Stand with your deputies.**
With gratitude,
**Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County**
---
|
---
| **P.S.** Write me back — just hit reply. I love reading your responses.

name: Bethany Mann for Congress
subject: Where's Dr. Bob? Meet the Congressman I'm Challenging
body:
Have you seen this Congressman? MO is still looking for him.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/14w8qlU5wr2?e=519ef02502&c2id=654d9c3339d5694b9267d382db7ced0e)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Friend,Whether you live here in Missouri's 3rd Congressional District or you're following our campaign from somewhere else in the country, I want to introduce you to the man I'm running against: Republican Congressman Bob Onder.
Onder currently represents Missouri's 3rd District in Washington, and his recent actions have raised important questions about how decisions affecting our communities are being made, who participates in those decisions, and what protections residents can expect.
That's why we're launching a video series called **"Where's Dr. Bob?"**
In our first installment, **"Who Gets a Seat at the Table?"** , we're examining three issues that deserve a closer look.
First, Congressman Onder has publicly discussed his conversations with President Donald Trump about redrawing Missouri's congressional districts. Redistricting determines which communities are represented together in Congress, making public transparency and accountability especially important.
Second, Onder has published an essay advocating major data center development in Missouri's 3rd District. At the same time, residents in communities including Montgomery County are raising concerns about the potential effects of these facilities on water resources, energy costs, farmland, and the environment.
Third, in February, Onder introduced H.R. 7554, legislation that would remove carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide from the Clean Air Act's definition of air pollutants. The proposal raises questions about the future scope of federal greenhouse gas regulation.
Specifically, those are the three gas pollutants produced in overabundance by data centers.
These are substantial policy decisions, with consequences that extend beyond Missouri.

# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142307361/656489102/-1160839820?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMDk3MjgyNi0zNGQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJkNTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=j3GcucajL5JJR6hfFTR776oH9ajobQe-0cGb9Kz4mwI=)
This is it, Peter. Seven days until Election Day, where voters across the 17th District will decide between two very different candidates to represent our community. Before we ask you to [**chip in $3**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142307363/656489104/-1160839820?refcode=em-10.27.26-all-1-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMDk3MjgyNi0zNGQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJkNTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=j3GcucajL5JJR6hfFTR776oH9ajobQe-0cGb9Kz4mwI=) to fuel our final get out the vote push, here's a side-by-side look at the decision voters have. **One the hand, you've got MAGA Republican Dillan Vancil.** Vancil has supported ICE raids that have killed innocent civilians, and even suggested we could use them in Illinois. He's also stood by Donald Trump as his reckless wars, tariffs, and corruption have made basic costs soar -- going so far as saying he's behind him, "100 percent." With him, we'd be closer to enacting the full Project 2025 that MAGA envisioned from the sart. **Our job over the next week is to make sure voters re-elect community weatherman and trusted Democrat Eric Sorensen instead.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142307365/656489106/-1160839820?refcode=em-10.27.26-all-1-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMDk3MjgyNi0zNGQyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJkNTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=j3GcucajL5JJR6hfFTR776oH9ajobQe-0cGb9Kz4mwI=) Eric was born and raised here, and has served his neighbors for over two decades delivering weather news. He takes his cues from _us_ , not the SuperPacs, which is why he supports reproductive rights, collective bargaining, protecting Social Security, and defending LGBTQ+ rights. Today is one week from Election Day, and Sabato's Crystal Ball just changed their rating of our race from "Toss-Up" to "Leans Democratic."
I'm still trying to wrap my head around how we got here.
The odds are still moving in our favor in a district Trump won by 18 points, but it'd be a big mistake to pull back now. **[Chip in now to help us build on our momentum and flip this seat in South Texas:](https://substack.com/redirect/7d875ad0-a745-45cc-91a1-0a551ceee3db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/7d875ad0-a745-45cc-91a1-0a551ceee3db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Saturday before early voting opened, I played the last concert of my career. Two days later, I voted for myself for Congress.
One night I'm on stage in my hometown saying goodbye, and the next I'm casting a ballot in the biggest race of my life.
_Unreal_ is the only word for it.
Early voting in Texas ends in three days, and every ballot cast before then is one we don't have to chase on Election Day.
We're running out of time to take the steps we need to flip TX-15 and the House along with it.
**So here 's my plan:** ads that answer the attacks, organizers knocking on doors across the district, calls to voters so the other side's ads don't drown us out, and rides to the polls for anyone who needs help getting there.
**[All of that takes resources. Will you give $5 today to help us reach as many voters as we can before Friday's early voting deadline?](https://substack.com/redirect/7d875ad0-a745-45cc-91a1-0a551ceee3db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you,
Bobby

Sabato's Crystal Ball just changed our race from "Toss-Up" to "Leans Democratic" Oct 27 | | | | | | | | | | | Today is one week from Election Day, and Sabato's Crystal Ball just changed their rating of our race from "Toss-Up" to "Leans Democratic." I'm still trying to wrap my head around how we got here. The odds are still moving in our favor in a district Trump won by 18 points, but it'd be a big mistake to pull back now. The Saturday before early voting opened, I played the last concert of my career. Two days later, I voted for myself for Congress. One night I'm on stage in my hometown saying goodbye, and the next I'm casting a ballot in the biggest race of my life. Unreal is the only word for it. Early voting in Texas ends in three days, and every ballot cast before then is one we don't have to chase on Election Day. We're running out of time to take the steps we need to flip TX-15 and the House along with it. So here 's my plan: ads that answer the attacks, organizers knocking on doors across the district, calls to voters so the other side's ads don't drown us out, and rides to the polls for anyone who needs help getting there. | 🇺🇸To all of Cait Conley’s supporters:💪 We ask you, humbly: Don’t click away from this email. This isn’t the first time we’ve emailed you about our final GOTV push, so we’ll get right to the point: We’re asking you to donate to Cait’s campaign today. The vast majority of people who read this email won’t give, though; they’ll look the other way. We’re hoping you’re different.
---

If everyone reading this donated literally $1, we wouldn’t just reach our goals. We wouldn’t just receive a huge number of donations. We would have the resources to turn out an absolutely monumental coalition on November 3rd. We’d beat Mike Lawler and take back the House.

Folks, we are one week out from Election Day and Donald Trump continues his crusade of election interference attempts. Look, let’s just be real about why he’s doing this. He’s desperately afraid of his party losing. And frankly, I believe that fear is well-founded. Their policies are deeply unpopular, they’re ignoring an affordability crisis that’s bankrupting families and starving children, and they can’t point to anything they’ve done to make life better for the American people. Now, Republicans are staring down a blue wave where they’re going to be thrashed at the polls. And these false claims and wild grasps — from the baseless lawsuit against California and the bogus lawsuit against Alaska to the threats to elections officials and everything in between — are all just a contingency plan for more desperate action they’ll surely take once they see the results. **But the facts and the law will always be our north star, and here in California we are fully prepared to stand up for the rule of law and the security, fairness, and accuracy of our elections.** Yesterday, we secured a critical early victory against Trump’s outrageous and completely unfounded lawsuit trying to interfere in California’s elections. A court denied the administration’s attempt to block California from counting more than 20,000 mail-in ballots. We’ll continue meeting the federal government in court to fight these baseless, desperate attempts to interfere with the upcoming election. And if they try to push conspiracy theories challenging election results they don’t like — as they did in 2020 when, you’ll remember, they lost every single case — we’ll meet them in court after the election, too. **We’re prepared. body:

|
# **Join Us in Los Angeles for the IPA Fundraiser**
---
|
---
| Autism Health Inc. is proud to support our friends and partners at **Informed Policy Advocates (IPA)** for their upcoming fundraiser on **Saturday, November 7, 2026, from 3:30 PM to 6:30 PM in Los Angeles, California**. As organizations committed to education, advocacy, transparency, and informed decision-making, Autism Health and IPA share a passion for empowering families and protecting the rights of individuals to make informed choices about their health and well-being. We value our collaboration and the important work IPA is doing to bring awareness to issues affecting families and communities. We invite our Southern California supporters to join us for an afternoon of connection, meaningful conversations, and fundraising in support of IPA's ongoing advocacy efforts. Your participation helps strengthen a community dedicated to making a positive impact through education and public engagement. **Event Details:** **Date:** Saturday, November 7, 2026
**Time:** 3:30 PM to 6:30 PM
**Location:** Los Angeles, California We look forward to seeing you there and continuing to build meaningful partnerships that make a difference!
---
| [REGISTER HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/TUXlWrmWCAm?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332 "REGISTER HERE")
---
|
---
|
# **Our Annual Gala has moved to California!**
---
|
---
| **New Venue, New Pricing, Same Powerful Mission!** We have some exciting updates to share about our upcoming **Transforming Lives Annual Gala: Lighting the Path to Solutions!** After careful consideration, we have made the decision to relocate our Gala from **Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida to Sherwood Country Club in Thousand Oaks, California.** This change allows us to significantly reduce event expenses, offer more affordable ticket pricing, and ensure that more of the funds raised go directly toward supporting individuals with autism and their families. We are thrilled to welcome you to an elegant evening of inspiration, connection, and purpose as we come together to advance research, education, and innovative solutions for autism. **Date:** Saturday, January 30, 2027 **Location: Sherwood Country Club**
[320 W Stafford Road](https://us.list-manage.com/iPWspOBumag?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332)
[Thousand Oaks, CA 91361](https://us.list-manage.com/eZL6vYLySuI?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332) **VIP Reception:** 4:00 PM – 6:00 PM
**General Admission:** 6:00 PM – 10:30 PM **Dress Code:** Formal Attire For a limited time, we're offering **exclusive Early Bird discounts on all tickets and tables!** Take advantage of these special savings now through November 30, 2026. **Prices increase December 1st!** **General Admission:** ~~$650~~ , **now $550**
_Save $100!_
**VIP Admission:** ~~$1,050~~ , **now $950**
_Save $100!_
**General Admission Table of 10:** ~~$6,000~~ , **now**** $5,000**
_Save $1,000!_
**VIP Table of 10:** ~~$10,000~~ , **now****$9,000**
_Save $1,000!_ **Don't wait! Secure your tickets or reserve your table today before Early Bird pricing ends November 30th!** We are honored to feature **General Michael Flynn, Del Bigtree, Dr. Sabine Hazan, and Dr. Brian Hooker** , with additional special guests and speakers to be announced. Guests will enjoy an elegant evening featuring exceptional dining, drinks, live entertainment, inspiring presentations, and exciting **live and silent auctions** , all while supporting a cause that is close to our hearts. **Sponsorship opportunities are also available for businesses and individuals who want to make an even greater impact.** Please contact Tracy For more information at [**tracy@autismhealth.com**](mailto:tracy@autismhealth.com). Thank you for your continued support, generosity, and belief in our mission. We look forward to celebrating with you in Thousand Oaks as we light the path to solutions and work together to transform lives!
---
| [BUY TICKETS HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/YIAq5psd8kS?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332 "BUY TICKETS HERE")
---
|
---
|
# **Join Us for the November Autism Support Group**
---
|
---
| You are invited to join us for our next **Autism Support Group on Tuesday, November 10th at 4:30 PM PST / 7:30 PM EST via Zoom**. Our monthly support group is a welcoming space for parents, caregivers, and families impacted by autism to come together, connect, and learn from one another. This is an opportunity to **ask questions, share experiences, hear parent testimonials, exchange resources, and receive encouragement** from a community that understands the challenges and victories that can come with the autism journey. At Autism Health, we believe families need more than information. They need **connection, support, and a community where they feel heard**. Whether your family is navigating a new diagnosis or you have been on this journey for many years, you are welcome to join us. **Advance registration is required to attend.** Once registered, you will receive the Zoom information for the meeting. We look forward to seeing you and continuing to build a strong and supportive Autism Health community!
---
| [REGISTER HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/4eDMKcUimJ0?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332 "REGISTER HERE")
---
|
---
| |
# **Early Bird Registration for the Autism Health Summit**
---
|
---
| The countdown has begun for the **2027 Autism Health Summit** , taking place **April 29 through May 1, 2027** , at **The Legacy Center Resort & Spa** in **San Diego, California**. Join parents, physicians, researchers, healthcare professionals, educators, and advocates from around the world for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and hope. name: Chris Pappas
subject: Azerbaijan
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9805%2E582294%2ESYKxaW ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9805%2E582294%2ESYKxaW ]Chris Pappas for Senate

At the GOP Senate debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he’s
running to send me back to “bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant.” He meant it as an insult.

As if the people who work in restaurants — cooking your food, clearing
your plates, keeping family businesses alive — have something to be
embarrassed about.

My great-grandfather came to New Hampshire from Greece over a century ago
and opened a candy shop in Manchester. My family built it into a
restaurant that’s been serving our community ever since.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261027_5.heXy-N&refcode=em20261027-5&t=1003&akid=9805%2E582294%2ESYKxaW ]Puritan Backroom sign

John Sununu was born into a political dynasty. His father was governor and
White House Chief of Staff. His brother was governor. John went to
Washington and then spent the next 17 years cashing in with Big Oil, Big
Pharma, and Wall Street.

Oh, and his family business invested in a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China. He’s never had to work hard a day in his
life — and his comments at that debate prove exactly what he thinks of
people who do.

The people who bus tables, flip burgers, and run small businesses in New
Hampshire don’t need a senator who looks down on them. They need one who
comes from them.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261027_5.heXy-N&amount=5&refcode=em20261027-5&t=1022&akid=9805%2E582294%2ESYKxaW ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. I do. That’s why I’m
running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261027_5.heXy-N&refcode=em20261027-5&t=1023&akid=9805%2E582294%2ESYKxaW ]Chris Pappas

subject: Here’s exactly what your $25 does
body:
Doors, gas, and boots on the ground.

---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter,
People ask me all the time: “Kailee, does my contribution REALLY make a difference?”
In a race this close?_**ABSOLUTELY, YES.**_
Races like NY-22 aren’t won by the side with the fanciest emails or tv ads. They’re won by SHOWING UP. The side that knocks the most doors, makes the most calls, and gets its voters to the polls.
_**That’s us.** But only if we can fund it._
**So here’s exactly where your money goes in these final days:**[**$25 → gets our message out there.** ](https://us.list-manage.com/HJgDAjXH7Rg?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)It helps us print materials, make phone calls, and push our ads.. [**$50 → fills a tank of gas.** ](https://us.list-manage.com/_Am7xlNbYS4?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)NY-22 is a big district. From Syracuse to the farm towns, we’re covering every mile.[**$100 → means 100 more doors knocked. **](https://us.list-manage.com/Y5pLmsNjNJn?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)One hundred more conversations with voters who could decide this race.
**Our FINAL fundraising deadline is midnight on October 31, the last one before Election Day.**
We’re within range of our goal, and we’re within range of FLIPPING this seat to give New Yorkers a voice again.
**I refuse to lose this race by a handful of doors we didn’t knock.**
Will you make sure we don’t, Peter?

Thank you for fighting alongside me.
Kailee Buller

---|---|---
A federal grand jury indicted Community Home Health Care LLC of South Portland, its owner Noora Abd, and five people who worked there on Oct. 22.
The co-conspirators behind the $50 million health care fraud are charged with conspiracy, while the Department of Justice also filed obstruction charges against Abd and Faysal Kalayaf Manahe, and a false-statement count against Mohammed Alkhalaf.
Although the company billed roughly $50 million from 2018 to 2025, according to state and federal Medicaid payment records, the federal indictment hinges on $600,000 worth of services that were billed for a single client but never provided.
[[RELATED: The Maine Wire's Seamus Othot was covering Community Home Health Care LLC back in April... Check out his reporting...]](https://substack.com/redirect/1dd2fe77-ea7e-4bc8-a502-31b2ea1d5797?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Prosecutors say Abd and Manahe learned of the FBI probe around June 23 and pushed a witness not to talk and to lie.
The charged amount is about 1 percent of Community Home Health Care LLC's total billing, but U.S. Attorney Andrew Benson dropped subtle hints during the press conference suggesting that the final arrest count could climb.
"I didn't want to comment on what the evidence may be at the time of trial, but you can use your own judgment in terms of what the evidence may be," Benson said Tuesday.
"The investigation does not end with today's arrests. It remains ongoing, and we encourage anyone with information to come forward and get in touch with us."
He called it "a complex, comprehensive investigation" that ran "several years."
The indictment itself leaves the door open. It says the defendants conspired "together and with others known and unknown to the grand jury." It describes services billed to "various MaineCare members, including Client 1," and says the scheme was meant to get paid for care not given "to clients of COMMUNITY, including Client 1." Two more people, "Person 1" and "Person 2," appear but aren't named. _Including_ is doing a lot of work there.
Community Home Health Care isn't the only Medicaid agency connected to the individuals indicted on Tuesday.
Manahe is listed in the federal provider registry as administrator of Decent Health Care LLC in Augusta. That agency had no state MaineCare payments through 2023. Then it drew about $1.1 million in 2024 and about $4.8 million in 2025.
DHHS listed Decent Health Care among the providers whose payments it suspended in June 2026 over credible allegations of fraud.
State corporate filings list the same Biddeford building as the registered-agent address for Community Home Health Care, for Decent Care Services LLC (agent: Faysal A. Kalayaf), and for two dissolved LLCs with Abd as agent.
Agents seized about $117,000 in cash and jewelry from a Biddeford address and about $54,000 from an Augusta address.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d101b48c-f891-4135-940c-2d29a5469566?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Hallowell property records show Noora Abd as the owner of these condos, which she purchased last year for $2.7 million cash
Just a few years ago, Abd, an Iraqi immigrant, listed her home address as a public housing complex on Mayo St. in Portland. Yet last year, Kennebec County records show she spent $2.7 million to purchase six condos in Hallowell, properties she still owns.
In addition to the various LLCs and other welfare agencies linked to Abd and her co-defendants, the group of Medicaid entrepreneurs also shared addresses with the Iraqi Cultural Association of Maine.
Manahe was listed as an officer with the nonprofit in 2020, according to tax filings, and the association listed the same office address as CHHC in South Portland. The association's mailing address is also linked to CHHC: it's 41 Cathedral Oaks Dr. in Biddeford, the same address where Abd reportedly lives.
* * *
Special hat tip to Seamus Othot of The Maine Wire who was all over this story back in April. Based on our investigation into records obtained under the Freedom of Access Act, Seamus visited the head office in April, where he was assured that the company was totally legit.

clean_body: | Hey, Peter! I have to be so honest with you — serving in Congress in the minority party has been exhausting. We’re fighting as hard as we can to deliver meaningful change when it comes to things like healthcare, affordability, and reproductive rights, but we keep getting blocked by the far-right Republicans who have the power. These are the sorts of things we can get done when we take back the House next month. I know things have been bleak, but with a Democratic majority in the House, we can finally pass nationwide abortion protections, get people back on their healthcare, hold ICE accountable, and be a hard check on Trump and his corruption. Your inbox is sure to be full of political emails right now and I’m sorry to add to that, but I am so hopeful about what we can get done starting in January if we can just get this win in November. = = = = = = There’s a future we can build when we win this election and we need every seat within reach to do it. — Emily If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please . | | Emily Randall is proud to represent Washington’s 6th District in Congress. I've skied the Wasatch my whole adult life, and I've never seen a winter like the last one. Temperatures ran way above average for weeks at a time. Snow that should have been piling up at 9,000 feet fell as rain. What falls on our mountains feeds the Colorado River basin and the taps of 40 million people across the West.
The Great Salt Lake kept shrinking, and every time the wind picked up, it lifted toxic dust off the dry lakebed and blew it toward two million people. In the valley, winter smog sat over Salt Lake like a dirty lid on a pot. You could taste it. Kids and grandparents felt it in their lungs first.
If we haven't met, I'm a professional ski mountaineer from Park City, and I've been with Protect Our Winters for more than 15 years. I was their first ski ambassador and the first captain of their ski team. I've testified before Congress on climate and public lands. On Sunday I'm running 26.2 miles through New York City for them, and every dollar you give helps POW fight for Utah's snow, air, and water. A gift of $26.20 is one dollar for every mile:
[Chip in here](https://substack.com/redirect/baa94b19-48de-4e08-b23b-0ad45a5c6820?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

I hand painted the VOTE on my NYC marathon outfit.
This year the Trump administration repealed the EPA's endangerment finding, the legal foundation that lets the federal government treat climate pollution as a danger to human health. It passed a tax bill handing oil and gas companies about $18 billion in incentives while cutting support for clean energy. In its first 100 days it took at least 145 actions to roll back environmental rules. Fossil fuel interests gave nearly $12 million to the inauguration fund before any of that happened. Then it came for Utah directly. In July the president cut Bears Ears and Grand Staircase down again, and mining claims were filed on the stripped land within weeks. Here at home, there's a push to fire old coal units to feed new data centers. Decisions like that get made when the rest of us aren't in the room.
The bill for all this doesn't come due in Washington. It comes due in places like Utah, and in places with far less. In late August, a flood tore through a Himalayan valleys near where I climbed and skied and killed nearly a thousand people in Nepal.
I won't pretend we're winning right now. We are losing ground this year in ways I didn't think possible. Some days it feels like a heavy pack I can't take off.
Running is how I set that pack down. When my feet hit the pavement, my head clears and my heart steadies. Running doesn't make the problem go away, but it turns worry into fuel. On Sunday morning I'll stand at the start on Staten Island with more than 60,000 other people. The clocks fall back that morning. I get one extra hour of sleep, and then I run 26.2 miles through all five boroughs for Utah's snow, air, and water.
We are not the underdogs we think we are. In a Yale poll this spring, about two out of three voters want the country running on clean energy by 2050. But researchers found that most Americans guess support is around 40 percent, when the real number is between 66 and 80 percent. So many of us want to move in the same direction. Running reminds us of that.
Protect Our Winters is how we get in the room. They take the love so many of us have for the outdoors and turn it into real power. They help people vote, speak up, and push for clean energy that means cleaner air and healthier towns. Two days after I cross the finish line in Central Park, Utah and the rest of the country go to the polls. The timing is not lost on me.
A marathon is won one step at a time, and so is this fight.
[Chip in here.](https://substack.com/redirect/baa94b19-48de-4e08-b23b-0ad45a5c6820?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Then run with me in two more ways. Tell me in the comments about the place in Utah or wherever you live that keeps you going, and I'll carry some of those places with me through the five boroughs. Share this with one friend who thinks they're the only one who still cares. And subscribe so you can follow along from the start line to the finish.
They can tear up the rules. They can't make us stop running.

clean_body: Our president is tearing up climate protections. Utah is already paying for it. On Sunday I'm running 26.2 miles for Protect Our Winters, and here's why I'm not slowing down. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Our president is tearing up climate protections. Utah is already paying for it. On Sunday I'm running 26.2 miles for Protect Our Winters, and here's why I'm not slowing down. | | | Oct 27 | | | | | | | | | | | | I've skied the Wasatch my whole adult life, and I've never seen a winter like the last one. Temperatures ran way above average for weeks at a time. Snow that should have been piling up at 9,000 feet fell as rain. What falls on our mountains feeds the Colorado River basin and the taps of 40 million people across the West. The Great Salt Lake kept shrinking, and every time the wind picked up, it lifted toxic dust off the dry lakebed and blew it toward two million people. In the valley, winter smog sat over Salt Lake like a dirty lid on a pot. You could taste it. Kids and grandparents felt it in their lungs first. If we haven't met, I'm a professional ski mountaineer from Park City, and I've been with Protect Our Winters for more than 15 years. I was their first ski ambassador and the first captain of their ski team. I've testified before Congress on climate and public lands. On Sunday I'm running 26.2 miles through New York City for them, and every dollar you give helps POW fight for Utah's snow, air, and water. A gift of $26.20 is one dollar for every mile: . | | ---|---|--- I hand painted the VOTE on my NYC marathon outfit. This year the Trump administration repealed the EPA's endangerment finding, the legal foundation that lets the federal government treat climate pollution as a danger to human health. It passed a tax bill handing oil and gas companies about $18 billion in incentives while cutting support for clean energy. In its first 100 days it took at least 145 actions to roll back environmental rules. Fossil fuel interests gave nearly $12 million to the inauguration fund before any of that happened. Then it came for Utah directly. In July the president cut Bears Ears and Grand Staircase down again, and mining claims were filed on the stripped land within weeks. Here at home, there's a push to fire old coal units to feed new data centers. Decisions like that get made when the rest of us aren't in the room. The bill for all this doesn't come due in Washington. It comes due in places like Utah, and in places with far less. In late August, a flood tore through a Himalayan valleys near where I climbed and skied and killed nearly a thousand people in Nepal. I won't pretend we're winning right now. We are losing ground this year in ways I didn't think possible. Some days it feels like a heavy pack I can't take off. Running is how I set that pack down. When my feet hit the pavement, my head clears and my heart steadies. Running doesn't make the problem go away, but it turns worry into fuel. On Sunday morning I'll stand at the start on Staten Island with more than 60,000 other people. The clocks fall back that morning. I get one extra hour of sleep, and then I run 26.2 miles through all five boroughs for Utah's snow, air, and water. We are not the underdogs we think we are. In a Yale poll this spring, about two out of three voters want the country running on clean energy by 2050. But researchers found that most Americans guess support is around 40 percent, when the real number is between 66 and 80 percent. So many of us want to move in the same direction. Running reminds us of that. Protect Our Winters is how we get in the room. They take the love so many of us have for the outdoors and turn it into real power. They help people vote, speak up, and push for clean energy that means cleaner air and healthier towns. Two days after I cross the finish line in Central Park, Utah and the rest of the country go to the polls. The timing is not lost on me. A marathon is won one step at a time, and so is this fight. Then run with me in two more ways. Tell me in the comments about the place in Utah or wherever you live that keeps you going, and I'll carry some of those places with me through the five boroughs. Share this with one friend who thinks they're the only one who still cares. And subscribe so you can follow along from the start line to the finish. They can tear up the rules. They can't make us stop running. | | ---|---|--- Caroline Gleich ⛰️ is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. | | Folks, there’s a Yiddish word that gets a lot of use in my house: kvetch. It means to complain. I’ve told my daughter since she was little that kvetching is OK, as long as you’re also working to fix the problem. With seven days until Election Day, it’s clear Jen Kiggans never got that second part. **She’s all kvetch, no action.** _She kvetches about the cost of living but hasn’t offered a plan to lower it.
She kvetches about “wokeness” to change the subject.
She kvetches about imaginary voter fraud instead of lifting the burden on Hampton Roads families.
She kvetches that this race shouldn’t be about Donald Trump, a month after taking his endorsement.
She kvetches about me instead of explaining her voting record to the people she’s supposed to represent. _ Voters here have noticed. ##### This week we handed it to Edgar Allan Poe. The free preview gets you the tariffs. Paid subscribers get the rest of the poem: the war, the gas pump, the measles, the machines, and the raven at the White House door with its one-word verdict.

_**-- Cliff**_
* * *
Once upon a midnight dreary, while the nation, weak and weary,
Watched the prices climbing upward in the markets and the stores,
I sat brooding, nearly broken, over promises once spoken,
Over golden words and slogans that had thundered through our doors--
Promises of cheaper living, peace and plenty, prosperous shores--
**Promises, and nothing more.**
Ah, I clearly can remember how Trump roared that cold November,
How he vowed to make us richer than we'd ever been before.
Tariffs, he declared, would save us, foreign rivals would behave us,
And the factories would return to fill our land with endless more.
But the price tags climbed like ivy, creeping higher than before--
**Higher still, and evermore.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ed5f5363-35a0-4bce-98d7-fbc3ed3d8d40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And the people stood bewildered as their grocery bills grew gilded,
While the cash they earned each Friday seemed to vanish by the score.
Eggs and butter, cars and clothing, every household budget groaning,
As the cost of common living crept beneath each kitchen door.
"Who will pay for all these tariffs?" cried the shoppers at the store--
**" Not the foreigners," came the answer. "You will pay for evermore!"**

body:
Three amendments are on your Tennessee ballot, and my guest Rep. Vincent Dixie and I are voting NO on every one.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/3c578e5dd2df/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363986?e=dc5f639d62)

Hey friends,Three amendments are on your Tennessee ballot, and my guest Rep. Vincent Dixie and I are **voting NO** on every one.
[CLICK HERE to LISTEN NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/VNI6dMwIsDj?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/t5P2WS3Bmfj?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**
Here’s the thing: the language you’ll see in the voting booth won’t tell you the whole story. Rep. Dixie of Nashville knows the bail system inside and out. He owns a bail bonding company, and he’s upfront about that, so you’ll hear it straight from someone who’s seen it up close.We dig into Amendment 1 and what it could mean for people who are accused but not convicted, for your county jail, and for your tax bill. We break down Amendment 2, the state property tax ban, and Amendment 3, the victims’ rights amendment. And we get into why policy doesn’t belong in our state’s Constitution.Your phone has probably been blowing up with questions about these. **Send this to someone who’s voting this week.****Here’s a quick look at why we’re voting NO:**
* **Amendment 1** takes away the right to bail for people accused of 73 felonies. That could mean months in jail before trial, and your county’s taxpayers footing the bill.
* **Amendment 2** bans a state property tax Tennessee doesn’t have. It won’t change your tax bill, and it limits what future lawmakers can do.
* **Amendment 3** adds victims’ rights to the Constitution that are already in state law and may affect due process rights.

**Early voting ends THIS Thursday, October 29** and Election Day is November 3. [**Find your polling location here**](https://us.list-manage.com/1A1vF8P0fxa?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0).
Thank you for being here,
Gloria

On Sunday, I shared with a group of folks that when we began this campaign, I knew that it was going to require me to work harder than I'd ever worked, to build a movement unlike anything else we've ever seen in East Tennessee, and bring in thousands of volunteers and supporters . . . and on top of that, we'd need a miracle.
And y'all, I think we might just experience a miracle in one week's time.
When we began this movement over one year ago, here's what I told you:
"This Congressional district is a Republican stronghold - arguably, one of the most reliable in the country. Last election, Burchett won with almost 70% of the vote. But this district, despite what anyone will tell you, is winnable."
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a926dc04-acf0-4068-9ce5-df2ad1a76e56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Austin East homecoming parade, Friday, October 23rd. Photo credit: Emery Ball_
I saw an opportunity to serve our neighbors and build a coalition of East Tennesseans, regardless of political affiliation, who wanted change. But I knew, as did you, how steep those odds were.
In the fall of 2025, I did __ believe that this seat was winnable - but I didn't know if we'd close that massive gap in one cycle. So much of it depended on what we built together, and on factors outside of my (and our) control.
After one year of hoping, working, and building, we are one week away from the most critical election of our lives. **And based on what I 'm seeing, we can flip this seat.**
Let me share a snapshot of what we've built over the last year, and what my team and I are seeing in the early voting numbers.
First, we've built a movement of hope I don't think many folks believed was possible in East Tennessee:
* $770,000+ raised
* 20+ East Tennesseans hired as staff on the campaign
* 1,300+ volunteers
* 19,000+ doors knocked
* 18,000+ postcards sent to voters written by volunteers
* 9,500+ voters called
* 4,000+ yard signs deployed around the district

That doesn't include the events and town halls we've hosted, the many causes we've supported through this campaign, the millions of people engaged on social media, and the community we've built.
Now here's what we're seeing in the data so far. **And here 's what I hope you take away: we can make the impossible possible. **_**But we need all hands on deck**_**.**
Based on the latest early voting data we have access to on the individual-level (October 24th), of those who have cast votes so far:
* 53.91% (46,480) are Republican
* 34.91% (30,097) are Democrats
* 11.17% (9,633) are non-partisan

In a typical year, about 28% of the non-partisan or Independent vote goes to the Democratic candidate. Based on that, our floor of the vote right now during early voting is 38%. (Keep in mind that on average, Tim Burchett gets about 68% of the vote compared to 32% for his Democratic opponent).
**But there 's nothing typical about this year, or this campaign.**
Nationally, the generic Congressional ballot has Dems up 11%. Here in East Tennessee, in the August election, mayoral candidate Beau Hawk swung roughly 12% of Republican primary voters. With a 12% swing among Republicans and Independents with Democratic turnout what it is right now, our model puts us at 45.85% of the vote.
Instead of looking at modeled individual partisan affiliation, we can also look at precinct turnout across the district. When comparing current turnout to 2022 early voting, 9 out of the 10 Knox County precincts with the highest share of early voters so far favor Democrats by at least 29%.
To be clear: early voting totals aren't election totals. Our model could be wrong . . . _**in either direction.**_
For the thousands of Democratic voters who show up during Presidential election years but not midterms, I'm putting out the bat signal.
For the Republicans and Independents who believe in this movement, I'm asking you to talk to your friends, coworkers, families, and neighbors.
For the people who have believed for a long time that their vote didn't matter, _**I 'm telling you it does.**_
If you're asking yourself: how do I help make history? Making history will require a historic level of effort, and we can't do it without you. We have action opportunities [every single day now through Election Day](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/01d261fb-e7f7-4dca-9de7-762aeb41c1e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
My field director shared that our biggest need this week is door-knocking. If every one of our volunteers signs up to do just one more canvassing shift between now and election day, _**we can talk to every Democratic voter in our key precincts who hasn 't voted yet and get them to the polls**_.
And on November 3rd, come to Printshop starting at 9 a.m. for [a day of action](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/cb1c89c7-181c-4f58-9b76-05398d0192a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (we will put you to work!) and our Election Night watch party after polls close.

Let's make history,
_**Michaela B for Tennessee**_

name: Mary Buell
subject: 7 Days Until Election Day — Make Your Voice Heard!
body:
Election Day is November 3! Learn where Jeff Walter stands on the issues that matter to Illinois families.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/jeffwalterforcongress/7-days-until-election-day-make-your-voice-heard?e=fa724b03ca)
---
|
---
| | | | | |

Friends,
**We are officially just 7 DAYS away from Election Day on Tuesday, November 3rd!**
This election is an opportunity to make your voice heard about the future of our country, our communities, and the issues that matter most to your family.
Jeff Walter, a businessman and U.S. Navy veteran running for Congress in Illinois' 11th Congressional District, has outlined his priorities for Washington:
* **Rebuild America's Economy:** Unleash American energy, reduce government red tape, and encourage the creation of good-paying American jobs.
* **Lower Taxes & the Cost of Living:** Address the rising costs of groceries, gas, and everyday necessities while providing relief to hardworking families.
* **Keep Our Communities Safe:** Support law enforcement, strengthen public safety, and hold criminals accountable.
* **Protect Social Security & Medicare:** Preserve the benefits that seniors have earned through decades of hard work.
* **Stop Wasteful Government Spending:** Eliminate fraud, reduce wasteful spending, and demand accountability for taxpayer dollars.

**With only seven days remaining, the campaign is continuing its final voter outreach efforts.**
If you would like to support these efforts, [please consider making a contribution](https://us.list-manage.com/1BSPWjISPqJ?e=fa724b03ca&c2id=02d8faed9a08421996be4d5fd2cd9a20) to Jeff Walter for Congress. [Donations](https://us.list-manage.com/HG3QAvHb36v?e=fa724b03ca&c2id=02d8faed9a08421996be4d5fd2cd9a20) help fund campaign communications, voter information, and other outreach activities during the final week.
**Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd, and every eligible voter has an opportunity to make their voice heard.**
Take time to review the candidates and their positions, make your voting plan, and encourage your friends and neighbors to participate.
Thank you for your engagement and support throughout this campaign.
**Mary Buell**
Campaign Manager
Jeff Walter for Congress

Last night I got to speak at a fundraiser for my friend Dan Schwartz.
Dan is running for Congress in Maryland's First District. The Eastern Shore. Andy Harris has held that seat for eight terms and wants a ninth. Harris is a member and staunch supporter of the Freedom Caucus. Most years he wins his races comfortably and nobody thinks twice. A Republican stronghold, they say.
Standing Our Ground is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..eBbioYsOPzLXsYQTMuRwkXgVpn0daaxFUWyNpP7kf_U?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=222394777)
Not this year.
Republicans are getting less popular everywhere, and you don't need a poll to see why. People can't keep up with the bills. Groceries. Gas. A mortgage. No relief anywhere in sight. And the Republican answer is trust us. Trust us, trust us, trust us. There's no plan. When there is something that looks like a plan, the rich get richer and the middle class picks up the check.
So when we take the majority back, we need more than a plan to stop Trump. We need a plan for people. Dan gets that.
The lineup last night: Governor Martin O'Malley. DNC Chair Ken Martin. Senator Chris Van Hollen. Congressman Jamie Raskin. And me. I'm still not over that, my voice amongst these great leaders in the Democratic party. Every one of them talked about how good Dan is at this, and I agree with every word.
Dan knows Social Security inside and out. He spent years in consumer affairs going after fraud. Real fraud, the kind that takes money from real people. Compare that to DOGE. Trump and Musk spent months telling the country they were hunting fraud, and what they mostly did was fire people who didn't agree with Trump. Dan did the actual work for years.
Now Andy Harris.
He doesn't hold town halls. On Oct. 13, after his debate with Dan, he told a student reporter from the University of Maryland that if she recorded him, he would refer her to prosecutors. Other people were recording. She was the one he went after.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/cc3066e1-84dd-486f-90b8-6cc7099e097e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Dan puts people first. Harris puts Donald Trump first. That's the whole story. He rubber stamps whatever Trump wants.
And for me, it's personal.
Since January 7th I've fought for accountability for what happened at the Capitol. For the rioters. For the organizers. For Donald Trump. Pardons took some of that away. The election took some more.
But nobody took away accountability for the people who pushed the big lie. Harris is one of them. He voted against certifying the election. He down played January 6th.
He was also one of the 21 Republicans who voted against the Congressional Gold Medal for the police who defended the Capitol. We got the medal anyway. But a man from Maryland, a few miles from that building, voted no on honoring the officers who protected him that day. I don't forget that.
One more thing about Dan. It tells you who he is.
Question 3 is on the Maryland ballot. If it passes, Maryland can redraw its map and make the Eastern Shore far more competitive, which effectively draws Harris's seat out from under him. Governor Moore backs it. Raskin. Van Hollen. Ken Martin. Barack Obama put out an ad for it this week.
Dan came out for it before he'd won a single vote. His reason was simple. It's not about my agenda. It's about what the people want.
That's the kind of member of Congress this district has never had.
I'm proud to stand with Dan Schwartz and I always will. Andy Harris has to go.
If you want to help, become a paid subscriber to Standing Our Ground. And if you live in Maryland's First District, vote YES on Question 3 and vote for Dan.
-Harry

Back in 2025, we promised we would center women in the fight to take back power. Today, with one week left until Election Day, we delivered on that promise. This is how:
**Mission Majority: The Path to Taking Back the U.S. House Runs Through EMILYs List Women**
In early 2025, our team put out the largest target map of any political organization. Pundits thought that our map was too aggressive and too ambitious — but we’ve watched race after race we identified become highly competitive. Now, polling is showing EMILYs List’s 26 Majority Makers running ahead or tied in “Toss-Up” races across the country. From top-tier battlegrounds to emerging seats where strong candidates and grassroots energy have put previously safe GOP held seats into play, all paths to the House run through EMILYs List women.
**Building the Road to a U.S. Senate Majority**
In the fight to take back the Senate, we can’t take any seats for granted. That’s why EMILYs List is supporting candidates running to hold critical seats for Democrats and flip Republican-held seats. These women are running from coast to coast, and they’re connecting with voters on the issues that will decide this election: lowering the cost of living, standing up for our fundamental freedoms, and taking on corruption.
**State Power Plan: Building Democratic Power in States Across the U.S.**
Our states have been a critical check against the Trump administration’s cruel MAGA agenda. But in order to counter Republicans’ partisan gerrymandering, preserve our healthcare, and make everyday life easier, we need to secure Democratic governing power in state and local office. That’s why EMILYs List recruited and trained strong candidates running to bring real change to their communities in nine key states: Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, New Mexico, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. These are states where EMILYs List women are running to break Republican governing trifectas, elect women governors, and build lasting Democratic power into 2028 and beyond.
The EMILYs List Campaigns team has been working day and night — digging into polls, data, and reporting. We’ve seen that this election has the potential to bring a sea change in power at all levels, fueled by voter enthusiasm and a desire for real change.
Now, with just a week left until Election Day, we have the chance to turn our plans into reality. This is the window where strategic investments turn into votes cast. When you donate, you’ll be joining the final push of paid media and organizing programs that will decide some of the closest races in the country. That’s exactly why we’re asking for your support.

| | I want to discuss what this election means for working families in Northwest Washington and across the country. **Costs continue to rise faster than paychecks.** Health care, housing, groceries, child care, and gasoline all take up more of a family's budget than they did a few years ago. For many households in our region, these are not minor inconveniences. They determine whether someone can afford a doctor's visit, stay current on rent, or keep up with the basic cost of getting to work. **This moment calls for a Congress willing to treat it as the urgent problem it is.** At the same time, folks are seeing an administration that has worked to undermine the Affordable Care Act, pushed tariff policies that have hurt farmers and small businesses, and taken actions that test the limits of our Constitution. These are not separate issues from affordability. **When health coverage becomes less secure, when tariffs raise the price of everyday goods, and when basic governing norms are ignored, working families are the ones who bear the cost.** This is why taking back the House matters. **A Democratic majority is necessary to hold this administration accountable, to protect the programs working families depend on, and to defend our democracy.** Without that majority, the damage already being done to household budgets and to our constitutional system will continue unchecked. clean_body: The damage already being done to household budgets and to our democracy will continue unchecked. | | | | I want to discuss what this election means for working families in Northwest Washington and across the country. Costs continue to rise faster than paychecks. Health care, housing, groceries, child care, and gasoline all take up more of a family's budget than they did a few years ago. For many households in our region, these are not minor inconveniences. They determine whether someone can afford a doctor's visit, stay current on rent, or keep up with the basic cost of getting to work. This moment calls for a Congress willing to treat it as the urgent problem it is. At the same time, folks are seeing an administration that has worked to undermine the Affordable Care Act, pushed tariff policies that have hurt farmers and small businesses, and taken actions that test the limits of our Constitution. These are not separate issues from affordability. When health coverage becomes less secure, when tariffs raise the price of everyday goods, and when basic governing norms are ignored, working families are the ones who bear the cost. This is why taking back the House matters. A Democratic majority is necessary to hold this administration accountable, to protect the programs working families depend on, and to defend our democracy. Without that majority, the damage already being done to household budgets and to our constitutional system will continue unchecked. In Texas, there’s no limit on what one billionaire can give. So we have to raise our goal.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I have to be honest with you about a change to our plan.

_**We just learned last night that Elon Musk gave Greg Abbott $5 million.**_

**So we don’t have a choice. We’re raising our goal for this week from $2 million to $3 million, to bring our October online fundraising total to $10 million.**
I wouldn’t ask if we didn’t need it. But this is an all-hands-on-deck moment, and I’m counting on people like you, not billionaires, to power this campaign.
[**Will you make your first contribution to this campaign right now? Even $15 will help us raise the extra $1 million we need to answer Elon Musk’s $5 million.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20261027_3_musk.0zCfqY&refcode=em20261027-2565&t=5&akid=2565%2E299639%2Eg6VD6o)

Gina

body:
Instead of following “business-as-usual,” I want to give you 3 things

| Peter, I don’t want to waste your valuable time, so I’ll let you know right off the bat that this is a fundraising email. [Read my 3 promises to you, and then decide for yourself whether it's worth giving $10.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.-DslOtkr1f8N7mA)
Peter, I witnessed firsthand how politicians make promises on the campaign trail, and the moment their plane lands in Washington, they immediately forget to act on those promises to the people. Instead of following “business-as-usual,” I want to give you 3 things I can promise you:
1. I promise to fight to ban congressional stock trading: My liberal opponent made over $21 MILLION trading stocks in Congress, and frankly, it’s beyond corrupt. As members of Congress, our job is to serve YOU, not our wallets.
2. I promise to fight to end congressional pay during government shutdowns: Government shutdowns are the result of partisan bickering, so if members of Congress can’t reach an agreement to fund the government, then we shouldn’t get paid – if we don’t do the job, we shouldn’t get paid!
3. I promise to fight for term limits: Serving in Congress should be serving your country – not creating a lifelong career out of it. Take Nancy Pelosi – she’s been in office for 39 years, serving the same lobbyists and big donors in Washington (not to mention trading stock and getting rich).
If you support my fight to clean up Washington, then [please consider chipping in $10 to support my campaign in this final stretch to Election Day.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)
---
| [HELP ME CLEAN UP WASHINGTON](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)
---
My liberal opponent called banning congressional stock trading “bullsh*t” – and she has Nancy Pelosi and Abigail Spanberger bankrolling her campaign. My opponent will fight to keep business as usual in Washington, so we CANNOT let her buy this seat from under us.
If there was ever a time to give, [it’s right now in these final weeks before Election Day.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)
-Jen Kiggans
---

I would not be where I am today without the help of my incredible and faithful supporters like you. Because of your support, I can keep fighting to make our country stronger.

Together we will get our country back on the right track and secure America’s success!

body:
7 days. One Senate majority. I’m not sitting this one out.
I’m not running this year. I’m campaigning like I am.

| | | |
---
| | | Fellow American, I’m not on the ballot this year. You’d never know it from my calendar. Friday, I gave the keynote at the Alaska Republican Party event in Anchorage to support my friend and colleague, Senator Dan Sullivan. Saturday, Dan Sullivan and I held **three get-out-the-vote rallies in a single day.** Before that, I was home in Texas, rallying with Ken Paxton in San Antonio and across the state. This year I’ve also campaigned for conservatives in Georgia, Iowa, Nebraska, and South Carolina. _And I’m not done._ North Carolina for Michael Whatley is next.Why am I doing this? Because right now, _there are 8 to 10 Senate races within the margin of error. _

**Peter, if this is the last email you see from my campaign, I’m okay with that. ** Laken Riley was murdered; that’s a fact. Her family begged for help, and I couldn’t sit on the sidelines; I wrote the law myself so the family of a murdered woman could get justice. Jon Ossoff voted ‘NO,’ and I looked him in the eye. He stared right through me. He was complicit in abandoning his duty to the people he’s supposed to represent.
He was complicit in letting justice slip through the Riley family's fingers. That’s who Jon Ossoff is. That’s his legacy. Unfortunately, Jon Ossoff’s friends in the Democrat party are more than happy to funnel money and support to a man who is willing to betray his constituents if it means currying favor with his overlords in the establishment. **That’s what we’re up against on Election Day.** Georgia has a choice: give a man who will stand by as the people he represents are murdered six more years in office, or change things for the better and elect someone who will actually fight for his neighbors. Jon Ossoff’s friends are funneling money into this race because they want the people of Georgia to forget that he said ‘NO’ when we demanded justice for Laken Riley’s life. _**I won’t let that happen. **_ I’m fighting like my life depends on it, because there were people whose lives were taken from them because Democrats like Jon Ossoff refuse to do what they promised and look out for the people who voted for them. I won’t make this some long-winded fundraising email, because I’m as mad as a wet hen. BUT the people of Georgia, and the people of America who could have been put in danger because of Jon’s policies are still out there, and they are in DANGER as long as Jon Ossoff can call himself a United States Senator. A few days ago, a reporter asked me what I thought of President Trump coming to Kansas to rally for my opponent, Sen. Roger Marshall. I told him I took it as a compliment, because it suggests our opponents are so scared Marshall might lose this race that _they sent the most powerful man in the country to try and save him._
**Well, you know what? I think they 're still scared** -- because they doubled down, sending JD Vance to Kansas yesterday (for his second visit) to try and rally support for Marshall yet again. And news just broke that President Trump is returning again on Oct. 31.
They may think that a few fly-ins from the president and Vice President will distract Kansans from the skyrocketing gas costs, out-of-control grocery prices and soaring energy costs they've been forced to endure under Roger Marshall.
**But as a fifth-generation Kansan, I know better -- and I bet you do too. **
I know the people of our great state are fed up and ready for change. I know they're ready for a leader who puts THEM ahead of party bosses -- who listens to them, thinks about ways to solve their problems and courageously fights to implement those solutions, even when doing so is hard.
Friends, I've listened to thousands of Kansans across the state talk about the challenges they're facing. They've told me how betrayed they feel by Marshall turning his back on them. They know he's nothing but a yes-man to his party and the president -- and they're suffering because of it.
I know Vance's visit is another attempt by the Marshall's allies to swoop in and prop up Roger Marshall. But I _also_ know that Kansans can see right through their scheme.
Here's the reality, though: Where the President and VP go, big money follows. The polls show this race is neck-and-neck and getting tighter every day. We've turned this into a toss-up race, and now, it all comes down to what we do in these final days. But GOP super PACs are pouring millions into this race -- and with just a week to go until Election Day, their attacks could turn undecided and swing voters against me at the worst possible time.
**That 's why, even though I know Kansans won't be fooled by these visits, I also know we have to respond. **We need to make sure our ads are in every living room in Kansas leading up to Election Day. We need to make sure our teams have the resources they need to knock on even more doors, make even more calls and put out even more yard signs. And we have to ensure every supporter has a plan to vote and knows what's at stake here.
All of these things take an incredible amount of resources. But with the help of people like you and the more than 100,000 grassroots supporters who have invested in this campaign, I know we can do it. And we must: This race is too important to lose.
**Friends, our opponents are running scared. Let 's show them they're right to be afraid -- and that their schemes won't work. At this critical time, every dollar makes a difference. Thank you for standing by my side.
Adam Hamilton
